QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r8.claim: Asil has the plurals asa’il and usul; min is partitive with a time expression, as in the verse under Nuh.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r8.anchor: على الظرف للتبعيض، كما دخلت على المفعول

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r30.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r30.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r30.claim: The surah closes with devotional practices, including invoking God's Names and listening to Quran recitation.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r30.anchor:
several verses dealing with pious and
devotional practices, including invoking the Names of God and
listening to the recitation of the Quran (vv. 180, 204–5).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.claim: The Prophet is urged to remain steadfast against opponents’ baseless objections and is shown what can help him persevere.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.anchor: At the end, the Prophet (sws) is urged to be steadfast in the wake of the nonsensical statements of his opponents and their baseless objections.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.claim: Remembrance should be inward, humble, meek, and fearful; arrogance and conceit are its opposites.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.anchor: it should be in one’s heart and should be with humility, meekness and fear.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.claim: If remembrance is audible, it should be moderate, as 17:110 directs; this also avoids adopting the idolaters’ way, since God hears and knows all.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.anchor: do not offer your prayer very loudly or in a very low tone; adopt a middle way between the two.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.speaker: the Prophet (sws)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.claim: The Prophet once stopped his companions from praying aloud.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.anchor: on one occasion, the Prophet (sws) had stopped his companions from praying in a loud voice.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.claim: Loud prayer can lead to pretension and showing off, both contrary to sincerity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.anchor: this may lead to pretension and showing off, which are totally against sincerity.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.claim: “Morning and evening” comprehensively covers all times, and the warning against indifference reinforces that remembrance should be continuous.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.anchor: The words “morning and evening” are meant to comprehensively cover all times.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.claim: As breathing sustains bodily life, remembrance sustains the soul; it is essential protection because Satan is always ready to attack.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.anchor: Just as for the life of the body, breathing is essential, in the same way, for the life of the soul, God’s remembrance is essential.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.claim: The form of remembrance may change with circumstances and needs, but it must never be forgotten, even for a moment, lest Satan attack.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.anchor: The form of this remembrance changes with circumstances and needs but it is not permissible to forget it at any instant.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.claim: Though singular in form, the address denotes a plural audience, as in verse 199.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.anchor: Though the address of the verse is in the singular, it denotes plurality, as in verse 199 earlier.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.claim: With two predicates coordinated after a negated predicate carrying bāʾ, genitive is preferred so both predicates match in case; the meaning remains clear.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.anchor: الوجه فيه الجر لأنك تريد أن تشرك بين الخبرين وليس ينقض ~~إجراؤه عليك المعنى

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.claim: He cites jarr by proximity in هذا جحر ضب خرب, while saying the present construction is also supported by its sound meaning.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.anchor: وقد حملهم قرب الجوار على أن جروا ~~هذا جحر ضب خرب ونحوه فكيف ما يصح معناه

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.claim: ʿUqayba al-Asadī's line uses accusative الحديدا by the underlying syntactic position after bāʾ, which adds no necessary meaning here.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.anchor: ومما جاء من الشعر في الإجراء ~~على الموضع قول عقيبة الأسدى

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.claim: The examples حسبك هذا and بحسبك هذا show that bāʾ can leave the meaning unchanged, so the phrase behaves as it did before bāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.anchor: ألا ترى ~~أنهم يقولون حسبك هذا وبحسبك هذا فلم تغير الباء

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.claim: After على, the coordinated عندنا must be accusative by position: it cannot be governed by على because عندنا functions only as an adverb.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.anchor: ولو قلت ما زيد على قومنا ولا عندنا كان النصب ليس غير لأنه لا ~~يجوز حمله على على

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.claim: He rejects بفوقه as an idiom after أخذتنا بالجود وفوقه and cites Kaʿb b. Juʿayl's ودون معد and al-ʿAjjāj's line as poetic parallels.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.anchor: ومثل ودون معد قول الشاعر وهو كعب بن ~~جعيل

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.claim: With كعمرو, accusative شبيها is good; genitive شبيه is used when the intended sense makes it dependent on the preceding kāf.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.anchor: وتقول ما زيد ~~كعمر و ولا شبيها به وما عمر و كخالد

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.claim: After بزيد, قريبا may be genitive under bāʾ or accusative by position; it can also function as an adverb.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسزيدبجبانولابخيلاوماز.anchor: وإذا قلت ما أنت بزيد ولا قريبا منه فإنه ليس ههنا معنى بالباء ~~لم يكن قبل أن تجئ بها

SIBAWAYH:والجرإنمايكونفىكلاسممضافإليه|وا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:والجرإنمايكونفىكلاسممضافإليه|وا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:والجرإنمايكونفىكلاسممضافإليه|وا.claim: A genitive complement is licensed in three ways: by a non-nominal, non-adverbial particle, by an adverbial noun, or by an ordinary noun.
SIBAWAYH:والجرإنمايكونفىكلاسممضافإليه|وا.anchor: المضاف إليه ينجز ~~بثلاثة أشياء بشئ ليس باسم ولا ظرف وبشئ يكون ظرفا

SIBAWAYH:والجرإنمايكونفىكلاسممضافإليه|وا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:والجرإنمايكونفىكلاسممضافإليه|وا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:والجرإنمايكونفىكلاسممضافإليه|وا.claim: دون is one of the locative adverbial nouns that governs a genitive complement; such forms are nouns used to locate things.
SIBAWAYH:والجرإنمايكونفىكلاسممضافإليه|وا.anchor: وقبالة ومكانك ودون ~~وقبل وبعد وإزاء وحذاء وما أشبه هذا من الأمكنة

SIBAWAYH:والجرإنمايكونفىكلاسممضافإليه|وا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:والجرإنمايكونفىكلاسممضافإليه|وا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:والجرإنمايكونفىكلاسممضافإليه|وا.claim: Particles such as bāʾ, kāf, min, and fī attach the preceding action or state to the following noun, as in مررت بزيد and أنت كعبد الله.
SIBAWAYH:والجرإنمايكونفىكلاسممضافإليه|وا.anchor: وأما الباء وما أشبهها فليست بظروف ولا أسماء ولكنها يضاف بها

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r1.claim: The preferred parsing makes تضرعا وخيفة purpose complements, since remembrance results from humility and fear.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r1.anchor: في نصبهما وجهان، أظهرهما: أنهما مفعولان من أجلهما لأنه يتسبب عنهما الذكر

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r2.claim: Alternatively, they are verbal nouns used adverbially as a circumstantial phrase: humbly and fearfully, or possessing humility and fear.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن ينتصبا على المصدر الواقع موقع الحال، أي: متضرعين خائفين، أو ذوي تضرع وخيفة

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r3.speaker: قارئ
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r3.claim: A variant reverses the fāʾ and yāʾ sequence, reading خفية.

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa calls both semantic verbal nouns rather than forms from the same lexical roots; the author considers this remote.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r4.anchor: وقيل: وهما مصدران للفعل من معناه لا من لفظه، ذكره أبو البقاء وهو بعيد

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa coordinates ودون الجهر with تضرعا, supplying a circumstantial meaning 'moderately'; the author calls it weak because دون is normally fixed as an adverb.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r5.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " معطوف على " تضرع " والتقدير: ومقتصدين ". وهذا ضعيف لأن " دون " ظرف

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes this a modifier of an omitted circumstantial phrase, meaning speaking below loudness; concealment better serves sincerity and reflection.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r6.anchor: فالذي ينبغي أن يجعل صفة لشيء محذوف، ذلك المحذوف هو الحال كما قدره الزمخشري فقال:

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r7.claim: The time phrase attaches to اذكر; الغدو and الآصال represent the day and night.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r7.anchor: قوله: { بالغدو والآصال } متعلق باذكر، أي: اذكره في هذين الوقتين وهما عبارة عن الليل والنهار

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa attaches بالغدو to ادعوا; the author calls this a slip because that is not the Qurʾan's word order here.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r8.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " بالغدو " متعلق ب " ادعوا " وهو سبق لسان وقلم، إذ ليس نظم القرآن كذا

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r9.claim: الغدو may be the plural of غدوة, with semantic coordination between two plurals.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r9.anchor: والغدو: إما جمع غدوة كقمح وقمحة، وعلى هذا فيكون قد قابل الجمع بالجمع المعنوي

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r10.claim: Alternatively, الغدو is a verbal noun with an implied time word, تقديره بأوقات الغدو.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r10.anchor: وقيل: هو مصدر فيقدر زمان مضاف إليه حتى يتقابل زمان مجموع بمثله

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r11.claim: One analysis makes الآصال a plural of أصل, itself plural of أصيل; it rejects direct pluralization from أصيل because فعيل does not form أفعال.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r11.anchor: والآصال: جمع أصل، وأصل جمع أصيل فهو جمع الجمع.

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r12.claim: A competing analysis allows الآصال as a direct plural of أصيل, since فعيل can form أفعال, as in يمين and أيمان.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r12.anchor: وقيل: بل هو جمع لأصيل، وفعيل يجمع على أفعال نحو: يمين وأيمان

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r13.claim: A third analysis treats الآصال as plural of أصل, singular for evening; this needs no plural-of-a-plural account, and the form also pluralizes as أصلان.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r13.anchor: وقيل: آصال جمع ل " أصل " وأصل مفرد، ثبت ذلك من لغتهم وهو العشي

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r14.claim: The poem وقفت فيها أصيلالا attests the diminutive; Kufans cite أصيلان for diminutives of broken plurals, while Basrans analyze it as a singular with nūn changed to lām.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r14.anchor: ويصغر على لفظه كقوله: 2378 وقفت فيها أصيلالا أسائلها

SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r15.speaker: أبو مجلز
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r15.claim: Abu Majliz (Lāhiq ibn Humayd) reads والإيصال, verbal noun of آصل, meaning to enter the evening.
SAMIN-DURR:7:205/r15.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز واسمه لاحق بن حميد السدوسي البصري " والإيصال " مصدر آصل، أي:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p229/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p229/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p229/r1.claim: The passage contrasts unbelievers, who humble themselves only in fear and disgrace on the promised Day, with believers who are humble in worldly life through faith, piety, and fear of God.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p229/r1.anchor: الكفار لا يكون إلا بعد أن يأتي اليوم الذي يوعّدون فيخشعوا خوفاًَ ورهبة وذلة، على حين يخشع المؤمنون في الدنيا، عن صدق إيمان وتقوى، وخشية لله

MALIK:8/r1.author: MALIK
MALIK:8/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
MALIK:8/r1.claim: Umar's letter sets the times for ʿAṣr and ʿIshāʾ; its closing warning against heedlessness applies the verse to observing prayer times. The collection states no grade.
MALIK:8/r1.anchor: أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، كَتَبَ إِلَى أَبِي مُوسَى الأَشْعَرِيِّ أَنْ صَلِّ الْعَصْرَ

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p246/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p246/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p246/r1.claim: Qatada says al-asal means the evening.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p246/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ بالغدو والآصال ﴾ قال الآصال العشي

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p248#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p248#2/r1.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p248#2/r1.claim: ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr reports that when a servant remembers God privately, God remembers him privately; when alone, God remembers him alone; when in a gathering, God remembers him in a better and nobler gathering.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p248#2/r1.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير في قوله تعالى ﴿ واذكر ربك في نفسك ﴾ قال يقول الله تعالى إذا ذكرني عبدي في نفسه ذكرته في نفسي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r1.claim: After commanding the audience to listen to Quran recitation, the passage turns to command the Messenger to remember his Lord.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r1.anchor: لما أمرهم تعالى بالاستماع والإنصات إذا شرع في قراءة القرآن ارتقى من أمرهم إلى أمر الرسول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r2.claim: Remember God inwardly, in a private state unseen by others, which he calls the highest and most noble state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r2.anchor: أي بحيث يراقبه ويذكره في الحالة التي لا يشعر بها أحد وهي الحالة الشريفة العليا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r3.claim: Remember God quietly, with humility and fear, without shouting or forceful projection, like one who quietly petitions a king for favors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r3.anchor: أي يذكره بالقول الخفي الذي لا يشعر بالتذلل والخشوع من غير صياح ولا تصويت شديد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r4.claim: When the companions raised their voices in supplication, the Prophet said they were not calling someone deaf or absent and told them to lower their voices; no grading is given.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r4.anchor: كما قال للصحابة وقد جهروا بالدعاء «إنكم لا تدعون أصم ولا غائبا اربؤوا على أنفسكم»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r5.claim: The companions spoke to the Prophet privately and softly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r5.anchor: وكان كلام الصحابة رضي الله عنهم للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم سرارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r6.claim: He invokes 49:4 and 49:2: calling loudly from outside the chambers showed poor judgment, and raising voices to the Prophet implied disregard, superiority, and lack of humility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r6.anchor: كما قال تعالى: إن الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات أكثرهم لا يعقلون وقال تعالى: لا ترفعوا أصواتكم فوق صوت النبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r7.claim: Dhikr includes declaring God's oneness, glorifying Him, and other forms of remembrance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r7.anchor: والذكر شامل لكل من التهليل والتسبيح وغير ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r8.claim: The two accusatives may be objects of purpose, since humility and fear motivate remembrance and relate to hope of reward and fear of punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r8.anchor: وانتصب تضرعا وخيفة على أنهما مفعولان من أجلهما لأنهما يتسبب عنهما الذكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r9.claim: Alternatively, the two verbal nouns function as circumstantial expressions: humble and fearful, or possessing humility and fear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r9.anchor: ويحتمل أن ينتصبا على أنهما مصدران في موضع الحال أي متضرعا وخائفا أو ذا تضرع وخيفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r11.claim: The apparent addressee is the Messenger; another view addresses every person who remembers, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the address is to him but extends to the whole community.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: خطاب له ويعم جميع أمته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r12.claim: The apparent object of remembrance is God Himself, since awareness of His sacred essence entails awareness of all His attributes; another view supplies an omitted word and means God's favors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r12.anchor: والظاهر تعلق الذكر بالرب تعالى لأن استحضار الذات المقدسة استحضار لجميع أوصافها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r13.claim: The title Lord carries honor and signals the beneficence of master to servants; it also fits the posture of servitude expressed by supplication and fear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r13.anchor: وفي لفظة ربك من التشريف بالخطاب والإشعار بالإحسان الصادر من المالك للملوك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r14.claim: The coordinated phrase “below loud speech” describes a state distinct from inward remembrance, since coordination implies difference.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p262/r14.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله «ودون الجهر من القول» حالة مغايرة لقوله في نفسك لعطفها عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r1.claim: The sentence may be part of the commanded speech, with واذكر coordinated to قل, or a fresh divine address to the Prophet that extends to every form of remembrance.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن تكون من القول المأمور به ويحتمل أن تكون إستئنافا من جهته تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r2.claim: Whether direct address or general instruction, inward remembrance is more conducive to sincerity and acceptance.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r2.anchor: وهو عام لكل ذكر فإن الإخفاء أدخل في الإخلاص وأقرب من القبول

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r3.claim: A divine saying promises that God remembers privately the one who remembers Him privately, and remembers in a better assembly one who remembers Him in a gathering; no source or grading is supplied.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r3.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار يقول الله تعالى : من ذكرني في نفسه ذكرته في نفسي

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r4.claim: The Imam explains inward remembrance as knowing the meanings of spoken invocations while recalling God’s perfection, power, greatness, and majesty; bare tongue-recitation without inward remembrance is nearly useless.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r4.anchor: قال الإمام : المراد بالذكر في نفسه أن يكون عارفا بمعاني الأذكار

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r5.speaker: جمع
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r5.claim: Some hold that bare verbal remembrance without attention earns no reward, and that one who says a good word without knowing or considering its meaning is not counted a believer before God.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r5.anchor: ذكر جمع أن الذكر اللساني الساذج لا ثواب فيه أصلا ومن أتى بالكلمة الطيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r6.claim: Another view addresses the Quran listener, takes remembrance as Quran, and commands the follower to recite quietly after the imam; Alusi considers this remote even if one accepts Abu Hanifa’s position.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r6.anchor: الخطاب لمستمع القرءان والذكر القرءان والمراد أمر المأموم بالقراءة سرا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r7.claim: تضرعا وخيفة may be circumstantial, meaning humbly and fearfully, or depend on an omitted noun meaning possessing humility and fear; purpose is not a suitable parse.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154/r7.anchor: في موضع الحال بتأويل اسم الفاعل أي متضرعا وخائفا أو بتقدير مضاف أي ذا تضرع وخيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r1.claim: Some parse this as a verbal noun for an unmentioned verb; al-Ālūsī rejects that analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r1.anchor: وجوز بعضهم كون ذلك مصدرا لفعل من غير المذكور وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r2.claim: Khīfa derives from khawfa, with the original wāw altered.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r2.anchor: وأصل خيفة خوفة ودون في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r3.claim: He parses “below loud speech” as an adjective of an omitted circumstantial object, with coordination to taḍarruʿan; dūn is usually noninflecting.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r3.anchor: صفة لمعمول حال محذوفة أي ومتكلما كلاما ما دون الجهر لأن دون لا تتصرف على المشهور والعطف على تضرعا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r4.claim: An alternative needs no ellipsis and takes the coordination with the circumstantial construction: remember humbly and moderately.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r4.anchor: لا حاجة إلى ما ذكر والعطف على حاله والمراد ذكره متضرعا ومقتصدا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r5.claim: Another analysis coordinates “below loud speech” with “within yourself”: remember inwardly and also with the tongue, without excessive volume.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r5.anchor: إن العطف على قوله تعالى : ( في نفسك ) لكن على معنى اذكره ذكرا في نفسك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r6.claim: Loudness means excessive raising of the voice; what is below it is still another kind of audible speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r6.anchor: والمراد بالجهر رفع الصوت المفرط وبما دونه نوع آخر من الجهر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the instructed volume as loud enough for the person to hear himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r7.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما : هو أن يسمع نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r8.claim: The Imam takes it as a middle volume between audible recitation and whispering, linking it to 17:110.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r8.anchor: الإمام : المراد أن يقع الذكر متوسطا بين الجهر والمخافتة كما قال تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the verse as addressing a congregant ordered to listen: remember inwardly and do not recite aloud.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r9.anchor: ويشعر كلام ابن زيد أن المراد بالجهر مقابل الذكر في النفس والآية عنده خطاب للمأموم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r10.speaker: القاموس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r10.claim: Al-Qāmūs treats ghuduw as the plural of ghudwah.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r10.anchor: بالغدو جمع غدوة كما في القاموس

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r11.speaker: الصحاح
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r11.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ defines ghuduw as the opposite of rawāḥ and gives the verb ghadā, yaghdu, ghudūwan.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r11.anchor: وفي الصحاح الغدو نقيض الرواح وقد غدا يغدو غدوا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r12.claim: Al-ghuduw means morning periods from the dawn prayer until sunrise; the time is expressed by the verbal noun, as in “I came at sunrise.”
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r12.anchor: أي بالغدوات جمع غدوة وهي ما بين صلاة الغداة وطلوع الشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r13.claim: If al-ghuduw is a singular verbal noun, an implied plural “times of morning” can make it parallel to al-āṣāl.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r13.anchor: وهو نص في أن الغدو مصدر لا جمع وعليه فقد يقدر معه مضاف مجموع أي أوقات الغدو

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r14.speaker: الأزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r14.claim: Al-Azharī analyzes al-āṣāl as the plural of aṣl, itself the plural of aṣīl, the time from afternoon prayer to sunset; this is a plural of plurals.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r14.anchor: كما قال الأزهري جمع أصل وأصل جمع أصيل أعني ما بين العصر إلى غروب الشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r15.claim: On this analysis al-āṣāl is not a paucity plural, nor a direct plural of aṣīl, since faʿīl does not normally pluralize as afʿāl.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r15.anchor: فهو جمع الجمع وليس للقلة وليس جمعا لأصيل لأن فعيلا لا يجمع على أفعال

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r16.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r16.claim: One view makes al-āṣāl a direct plural of aṣīl, citing the pattern in yamīn and aymān.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r16.anchor: وقيل : إنه جمع له لأنه قد يجمع عليه كيمين وأيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r17.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r17.claim: Another view makes it the plural of a singular aṣl, compared with ʿunuq and its plural aṣlān.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r17.anchor: وقيل : إنه جمع لأصل مفردا كعنق ويجمع على أصلان أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r18.claim: The prepositional phrase is attached to “remember.”
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r18.anchor: والجار متعلق باذكر وخص هذان الوقتان بالذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r19.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r19.claim: Morning and evening mark opposite transitions: sleep like death gives way to waking like life, darkness to light, and evening reverses the movement.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r19.anchor: لأن الغدوة عندها ينقلب الحيوان من النوم الذي هو كالموت إلى اليقظة التي هي كالحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r20.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r20.claim: These are free periods, when remembrance is more likely to occupy the heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r20.anchor: أو لأنهما وقتا فراغ فيكون الذكر فيهما ألصق بالقلب

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r21.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r21.claim: The two periods are specified because angels take turns over a person then.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r21.anchor: وقيل : لأنهما وقتان يتعاقب فيهما الملائكة على ابن آدم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r22.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r22.claim: The times are not restrictive; they signal remembrance that continues at every time.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r22.anchor: وقيل : ليس المراد التخصيص بل دوام الذكر واتصاله أي اذكر كل وقت

ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r23.speaker: أبو مجاز لاحق بن حميد السدوسي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r23.claim: Abū Majāz reads al-īṣāl, a verbal noun for entry into evening, parallel to ghuduw on the singular verbal-noun analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p154#2/r23.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجاز لاحق بن حميد السدوسي ( والإيصال ) وهو مصدر آصل

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155/r1.claim: The warning is against being among those heedless of remembrance of God.

BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r1.claim: The Persian gloss says some who reach sincerity and purify their inward selves of ostentation practice loud remembrance; both groups have proofs for their practice.
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r1.anchor: كه بمرتبه اخلاص رسيدند وباطن خودرا از ريا اك يا فتند ذكررا بجهر كفتند

BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r2.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r2.claim: The Mathnawī urges calling on God in lament so the friend's grace may appear, and keeping thirsty for the divine gift.
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r2.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : كفت ادعوا الله بي زاري مباش

BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r3.speaker: عمر
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r3.claim: ʿUmar reports that the Prophet would not lower his hands after supplication before wiping his face with them.
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r3.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "إذا رفع يديه في الدعاء

BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r4.claim: The author connects the prayer mark on the face to 48:29 and says the wiping brings blessing from the hands to the face.

BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r5.claim: In the inward explanation, supplication turns the person outwardly and inwardly toward God and therefore requires an attentive heart; the raised hands represent these two orientations, the tongue the whole person, and wiping the face a return to the reality joining spirit and body.
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r5.anchor: إن الإنسان حال دعائه متوجه إلى الله تعالى بظاهره وباطنه

BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r6.speaker: الأسرار المحمدية
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r6.claim: The Asrār Muḥammadiyya prescribes spreading the palms skyward for a request, raising the arms before the face in distress, turning the backs of the hands skyward when praying against someone, and uncovering the hands from sleeves.
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r6.anchor: وقال أيضا : السنة للداعي في طلب الحاجة له أن ينشرهما

BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r7.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r7.claim: Abū Yazīd al-Bisṭāmī dreamed that his exposed hand was filled with light while the hand hidden from the cold remained empty; the divine voice said the hand offered in asking was filled.
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r7.anchor: قال سلطان العارفين أبو يزيد البسطامي : دعوت الله ليلة فأخرجت إحدى يدي

BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r8.claim: Raising the hands and looking upward while praying resembles a petitioner pointing to a sultan's treasury and asking him to pour out its gifts.
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r8.anchor: ورفع الأيدي إلى السماء والنظر إليها وقت الدعاء بمنزلة

BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r9.claim: Because provision and promise are in heaven (51:22), heaven is the direction of prayer and the place from which blessings descend; the best posture spreads both palms with a gap between them.
BURSEVI:v3p134#2/r9.anchor: فالسماء قبلة الدعاء ومحل نزول البركات والأفضل أن يبسط كفيه

BURSEVI:v3p233/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p233/r5.claim: The command may address Muhammad specifically or all people; remembrance drives away heedlessness, absent in Paradise because its people remain present with God.
BURSEVI:v3p233/r5.anchor: {واذكر} يا محمد. {ربك} ويجوز أن يكون المراد جميع الخلق والذكر طرد الغفلة ولذا لا يكون في الجنة لأنها مقام الحضور الدائم.

BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r1.claim: Remembering inwardly means quiet speech, which better protects sincerity and invites response; it includes recitation, supplication, and every form of obedience.
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r1.anchor: {فى نفسك} وهو الذكر بالكلام الخفي فإن الإخفاء أدخل في الإخلاص وأقرب من الإجابة وهذا الذكر يعم الأذكار كلها من القراءة والدعاء وغيرها

BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r2.claim: Tadharruʿan is a verbal noun serving as a circumstantial accusative for the subject of “remember”: remember humbly and submissively.
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r2.anchor: {تضرعا} مصدر واقع موقع الحال من فاعل اذكر أي متضرعا ومتذللا.

BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r3.claim: Ḍarāʿa means humility, abasement, and surrender; imploring God means beseeching Him humbly, while ibtihāl is earnest, sincere supplication.
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r3.anchor: والضراعة الخضوع والذل والاستكانة يقال تضرع إلى الله أي ابتهل وتذلل والابتهال الاجتهاد في الدعاء وإخلاصه.

BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r4.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r4.claim: A gnostic says prayer is the best bodily movement, fasting the best stillness, and supplication within worship unties what the revolving spheres have bound.
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r4.anchor: قال بعض العارفين ، بالله : الصلاة أفضل الحركات ، والصوم أفضل السكنات ، والتضرع في هياكل العبادات يحل ما عقدته الأفلاك الدائرات.

BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r5.claim: The cited poem says that if divine generosity had not intended to grant the request, it would not have taught the petitioner to ask.
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r5.anchor: لو لم ترد نيل ما أرجو وأطلبه

BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r6.claim: Khīfatan is pronounced with kasra; khawfah changes wāw to yāʾ after a kasra, and the word means remembering while afraid.
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r6.anchor: {وخيفة} بكسر الخاء أصلها خوفة قلبت الواو ياء لسكونها وانكسار ما قبلها أي وحال كونك خائفا.

BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r7.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says fear includes falling short in deeds, fear of one’s ending, and fear of the prior decree; the ending follows what was decreed, as the Prophet said the Pen is dry until resurrection.
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : وهذا الخوف يتناول خوف التقصير في الأعمال وخوف الخاتمة

BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r8.claim: The author limits fear of one’s end and prior decree to the community; prophets and perfected saints are safe from that fear, though they have another fear suited to their rank.
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r8.anchor: يقول الفقير : هذا بالنسبة إلى أن يكون المراد بالخطاب في الآية هو الأمة وإلا فالأنبياء بل وكمل الأولياء آمنون به من خوف الخاتمة والفاتحة

BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r9.claim: Human perfection manifests God’s lordly majesty and the servant’s lowliness; remembrance serves the first aim, while humility and fear serve the second.
BURSEVI:v3p233#2/r9.anchor: ولما كان أكمل أحوال الإنسان أن يظهر عزة ربوبية الله وذلة عبودية نفسه أمر الله بالذكر ليتم المقصود الأول وقيده بالتضرع والخيفة

BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r1.claim: “Below loud speech” describes an implied state: speak quietly enough to aid reflection; an imam in an audible prayer should use only enough volume for the congregation.
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r1.anchor: {ودون الجهر من القول} صفة لمحذوف هو الحال أي ومتكلما كلاما هو دون الجهر فإنه أقرب إلى حسن التفكر فمن أم في صلاة الجهر ينبغي له أن لا يجهر جهرا شديدا

BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r2.speaker: الكشف
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r2.claim: Al-Kashf says not to raise the voice beyond people’s need; doing so is misconduct, and he calls disapproval more serious than mere offense.
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r2.anchor: قال في "الكشف" : لا يجهر فوق حاجة الناس وإلا فهو مسيء. والفرق بين الكراهة والإساءة هو أن الكراهة أفحش من الإساءة

BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r3.speaker: عمر وأبو بكر
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r3.claim: When Umar recited loudly to wake sleepers and drive off Satan, the Prophet told him to lower his voice; when Abu Bakr recited softly, he told him to raise it slightly.
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r3.anchor: ولما رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عمر رضي الله عنه يقرأ رافعا صوته فسأله فقال أوقظ الوسنان وأطرد الشيطان قال عليه السلام : "اخفض من صوتك قليلا"

BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r4.speaker: النووي
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r4.claim: Al-Nawawi reconciles reports favoring quiet and audible remembrance: conceal it when ostentation or disturbance is feared; otherwise audibility benefits listeners, focuses and energizes the reciter, and dispels sleep.
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r4.anchor: وقد جمع النووي بين الأحاديث الواردة في استحباب الجهر بالذكر والواردة في استحباب الإسرار به بأن الإخفاء أفضل حيث خاف الرياء أو تأذى المصلون أو النائمون

BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r5.speaker: أنوار المشارق
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r5.claim: Anwar al-Mashariq says excessive loudness in prayer and takbīr is disliked; moderate volume with humility and no ostentation is permitted by scholarly agreement.
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r5.anchor: وبالجملة إن المختار عند الاخيار أن المبالغة والاستقصاء في رفع الصوت بالتكبير في الصلاة ونحوه مكروه والحالة الوسطى بين الجهر والإخفاء

BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r6.speaker: شارح الكشاف
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r6.claim: The Kashshaf commentator says a spiritual guide may tell a beginner to raise his voice to uproot entrenched thoughts.
BURSEVI:v3p233#3/r6.anchor: وقد سبق من شارح "الكشاف" أن الشيخ المرشد قد يأمر المبتدي برفع الصوت لتنقلع من قلبه الخواطر الراسخة فيه.

BURSEVI:v3p234/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p234/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p234/r1.claim: The time phrase attaches to “remember”: ghudū is the morning interval between dawn prayer and sunrise; āṣāl is plural of aṣīl, after afternoon prayer until sunset, while ʿashī runs from sunset to night.
BURSEVI:v3p234/r1.anchor: فإن الغدو جمع غدوة وهي ما بين صلاة الغداة وطلوع الشمس

BURSEVI:v3p234/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p234/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p234/r2.claim: These hours display astonishing changes in the world, proving its wise and powerful God; witnesses should remember Him humbly and fear their own circumstances turning bad.
BURSEVI:v3p234/r2.anchor: وخص هذان الوقتان لأن فيهما تتغير أحوال العالم تغيرا عجيبا يدل على أن المؤثر فيه هو الإله الموصوف بالحكمة الباهرة والقدرة القاهرة

BURSEVI:v3p234/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p234/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p234/r3.claim: Another view takes morning and evening as figures for day and night, named by their endpoints, and calls for remembering God continually as far as possible.
BURSEVI:v3p234/r3.anchor: وقيل : الغدو والآصال عبارتان عن الليل والنهار اكتفى عن ذكرهما بذكر طرفيهما والمراد بذكره تعالى فيهما المواظبة عليه بقدر الإمكان.

BURSEVI:v3p234/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p234/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p234/r4.claim: After commanding remembrance with awareness of what the tongue says, God forbids the heart from becoming heedless of His majesty and grandeur.
BURSEVI:v3p234/r4.anchor: ثم أتبعه بقوله : {ولا تكن من الغافلين} للدلالة على أن الإنسان ينبغي له

BURSEVI:v3p234/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p234/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p234/r5.claim: A prophetic report calls remembrance better than meeting enemies in battle; jihad and martyrdom lead to Paradise, while the rememberer is God’s companion and witnesses Him, a greater gift than Paradise itself.
BURSEVI:v3p234/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث : "ألا أنبئكم بما هو خير لكم وأفضل من أن تلقوا عدوكم فتضربوا رقابهم ويضربوا رقابكم ذكر الله" أي : ما هو خير لكم

BURSEVI:v3p234/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p234/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p234/r6.claim: The saying “I am the companion of whoever remembers Me” grounds the author’s claim that remembrance brings divine presence and witnessing, while vision comes after entrance into Paradise.
BURSEVI:v3p234/r6.anchor: كما قال : "أنا جليس من ذكرني" والجليس لا بد أن يكون مشهودا فالحق مشهود الذاكر وشهود الحق أفضل من حصول الجنة ولذلك كانت الرؤية بعد حصول الجنة

BURSEVI:v3p234/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p234/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p234/r7.claim: Proper remembrance uses the tongue while heart, spirit, and all faculties remain present and wholly turned to God, silencing passing thoughts and inner talk.
BURSEVI:v3p234/r7.anchor: والذكر المطلوب من العبد ، أن يذكر الله باللسان ويكون حاضرا بقلبه وروحه وجميع قواه بحيث يكون بالكلية متوجها إلى ربه فتنتفي الخواطر وتنقطع أحاديث النفس عنه.

BURSEVI:v3p234/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p234/r8.speaker: داود القيصري
BURSEVI:v3p234/r8.claim: Qaysari describes dhikr moving from tongue to heart and eventually unveiling divine manifestations of attributes, names, and essence; the servant is effaced, God remembers Himself, and duality gives way to oneness, illuminated by 14:48.
BURSEVI:v3p234/r8.anchor: ثم إذا داوم عليه ينتقل الذكر من لسانه إلى قلبه ولا يزال يذكر بذلك حتى يتجلى له الحق من وراء أستاء غيوبه

DURR-FULL:v3p637/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r4.claim: Qatada says God commands remembrance and forbids heedlessness; dawn means the dawn prayer, al-asal the evening.
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: أمره الله أن يذكره ونهاه عن الغفلة

DURR-FULL:v3p637/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r5.speaker: أبو صخر
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r5.claim: Abu Sakhr says al-asal is the period between noon and afternoon.
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r5.anchor: عن أبي صخر قال: الآصال: ما بين الظهر والعصر

DURR-FULL:v3p637/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd links listening to the imam beginning prayer, then addresses the listener to remember God inwardly, humbly and fearfully, without loudness; dawn and al-asal mean morning and evening.
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r6.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا}

DURR-FULL:v3p637/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r7.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r7.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr transmits God’s promise to remember the servant as the servant remembers Him: inwardly, privately, or in a better and nobler gathering.
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r7.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير في قوله {واذكر ربك في نفسك} قال: يقول الله

DURR-FULL:v3p637/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r8.claim: Mujahid identifies dawn with the end of the dawn prayer and al-asal with the end of the afternoon prayer, and links the wording to 3:41.
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد {بالغدو} قال: آخر الفجر صلاة الصبح

DURR-FULL:v3p639/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r1.speaker: أبو وائل
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r1.claim: Abu Waʾil used آصلنا for sunset, illustrating al-asal usage.
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r1.anchor: عن معرف بن واصل قال: سمعت أبا وائل يقول لغلامه عند مغيب الشمس: آصلنا

DURR-FULL:v3p639/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r2.claim: The Prophet compares someone remembering God among the heedless to a fighter defending the two groups.
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله {ولا تكن من الغافلين} قال: ذاكر الله

DURR-FULL:v3p639/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r3.speaker: بكير بن الأخنس
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r3.claim: Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas says anyone reaching Friday without knowing it is Friday is counted among the heedless.
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r3.anchor: عن بكير بن الأخنس قال: ما أتى يوم الجمعة على أحد وهو لا يعلم

DURR-FULL:v3p639/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r4.claim: The Prophet identifies three heedlessnesses: neglecting God’s remembrance, the period from dawn prayer to sunrise, and neglecting one’s religious self until it is overtaken.
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمرو أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: الغفلة في ثلاث

BURSEVI:v3p235/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235/r1.speaker: ابن ملك
BURSEVI:v3p235/r1.claim: Ibn Malik says a regularly sustained practice is beloved because the soul grows accustomed to it and thereby keeps turning toward God; Sufis likewise condemn abandoning litanies and obligations.
BURSEVI:v3p235/r1.anchor: قال ابن ملك : وإنما كان العمل الذي يداوم عليه أحب لأن النفس تألف به ويدوم بسببه الإقبال على الله تعالى ولهذا ينكر أهل التصوف ترك الأوراد كما ينكرون

BURSEVI:v3p235/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء بالله
BURSEVI:v3p235/r2.claim: A knower of God calls only the ignorant one who belittles a devotional litany: its afterlife reward follows the practice, which ends with this world.
BURSEVI:v3p235/r2.anchor: قال بعض العلماء بالله : لا يستحقر الورد إلا جهول

BURSEVI:v3p235/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p235/r3.claim: A hadith says God admits people to Paradise by mercy and apportions its rewards by deeds; the author says the litany's reward is lost when the worldly practice ends.
BURSEVI:v3p235/r3.anchor: إن الله تعالى يقول ادخلوا الجنة برحمتي وتقاسموها بأعمالكم

BURSEVI:v3p235/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p235/r4.claim: Serve the Master by keeping the litany for God's right and seek steadfastness rather than wonders; the soul wants extraordinary gifts, while God asks for constancy.
BURSEVI:v3p235/r4.anchor: فطب نفسا بالعمل لمولاك وسلم له فيما به يتولاك فقد قالوا كن طالب الاستقامة ولا تكن طالب الكرامة فإن نفسك تهتز وتطلب الكرامة ومولاك يطالبك بالاستقامة

BURSEVI:v3p235/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235/r5.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v3p235/r5.claim: Hafiz's couplet says companionship of houris is a shortcoming compared with the beloved, illustrating preference for divine intimacy over Paradise's attractions.
BURSEVI:v3p235/r5.anchor: قال الحافظ : صحبت حور نخواهم كه بود عين قصور

BURSEVI:v3p235/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p235/r6.claim: Citing al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya, the author reads inward remembrance as replacing the self's actions with commanded deeds, character with divine character, and essence with effacement in God; a sacred report and 2:152 express reciprocal remembrance, illustrated by moth and candle.
BURSEVI:v3p235/r6.anchor: {واذكر ربك في نفسك} أي : اذكره بالأفعال والأخلاق والذات في نفسك

BURSEVI:v3p235/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p235/r7.claim: The three phrases map sharia's outward effort to alter acts, tariqa's inward adoption of divine manners, then self-effacement through the lights of truth and silence about the lordly secret.
BURSEVI:v3p235/r7.anchor: التضرع من باب التكلف أي بداية هذا الذكر بتبديل أفعال النفس بأعمال الشريعة تكون بالتكلف ظاهرة

BURSEVI:v3p235/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235/r8.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v3p235/r8.claim: The cited prophetic saying calls disclosure of the secret of lordship unbelief.

BURSEVI:v3p235/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p235/r9.claim: Dawn and evening signify primordial beginning and endless eternity: God alone is the true rememberer and remembered, having remembered humanity in pre-eternity.
BURSEVI:v3p235/r9.anchor: {بالغدو والاصال} يشير إلى غدو الأزل وآصال الأبد

BURSEVI:v3p235/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235/r10.speaker: يوسف بن حسين الرازي
BURSEVI:v3p235/r10.claim: Ibn Husayn al-Razi says no one remembers God except God; the heedless fail to recognize that God is truly both the rememberer and the remembered.
BURSEVI:v3p235/r10.anchor: قول يوسف بن حسين الرازي ما ذكر أحد الله إلا الله

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r1.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r1.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr relates God's promise to remember the servant who remembers Him, privately when private and before a better, more honored company when in a gathering.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r1.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير في قول الله : واذكر ربك في نفسك قال : يقول الله : اذا ذكرني عبدي في نفسه ذكرته في نفسي

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r2.claim: Qatada says God commands remembrance and forbids heedlessness.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة امر الله بذكره ونهى عن الغفلة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam explains remembrance as remembering God, glorifying Him, declaring His oneness, and praising Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r3.anchor: عن أبيه زيد بن اسلم واذكر ربك في نفسك قال : الذكر ان تذكر الله وتسبحه وتهلله وتحمده

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r4.speaker: الحكم بن عتيبة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r4.claim: Al-Hakam ibn Utayba says that when one hears the imam recite, one should not utter anything.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r4.anchor: عن مطرف عن الحكم ابن عتيبة في قوله : واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة قال : اذا اسمعك الامام القراءة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the instruction as not reciting aloud.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r5.anchor: سمعت ابن زيد في قوله : ودون الجهر من القول لا تجهر بذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says not to recite aloud at dawn or in the late afternoon.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r6.anchor: عن أبيه زيد بن اسلم دون الجهر من القول قال : لا تجهر بالغدو والاصال

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r7.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r7.claim: A further report from Zayd ibn Aslam says there is audible recitation at dawn.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r7.anchor: وباسناده قال : ودون الجهر من القول بالغدو يجهر فيها

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r8.claim: Qatada identifies dawn as the morning prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r8.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : بالغدو قال : اما بالغدو فصلاة الصبح

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r9.claim: Qatada glosses the late-afternoon periods as evening.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r9.anchor: وبه عن قتادة والاصال قال : بالعشى

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r10.speaker: أبو صخر
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r10.claim: Abu Sakhr defines al-asal as the period between noon and afternoon.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1647/r10.anchor: عن أبي صخر في قوله : بالغدو والاصال والاصال ما بين الظهر والعصر

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1648/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1648/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1648/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam glosses the warning as not being among the heedless.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1648/r1.anchor: وبه عن ابن زيد ، عن أبيه اسلم قال : ولا تكن من الغافلين قال : مع الغافلين

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1648/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1648/r2.speaker: بكير بن الأخنس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1648/r2.claim: Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas says anyone who reaches Friday without knowing it is Friday is counted among the heedless.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1648/r2.anchor: عن عمرو بن مرة ، عن بكير بن الاخنس قال : ما اتى يوم الجمعة على أحد وهو لا يعلم انه يوم جمعة الا كتب من الغافلين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r1.claim: After the commands the Prophet must convey, the discourse turns to his own devotion; asking people to hear the Qur'an implies his reciting it aloud, then his own remembrance is addressed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r1.anchor: إقبال بالخطاب على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما يختص به ، بعد أن أمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r2.claim: Nafs can mean the life-giving soul, the embodied self, inner cognition, or a person's private self; 5:116 uses it for what lies within, and the Bukhari hadith contrasts it with a public gathering.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r2.anchor: ولكون مقر النفس في باطن الإنسان أطلقت على أمور باطن الإنسان من الإدراك والعقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r3.speaker: الله تعالى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r3.claim: A hadith qudsi in Sahih al-Bukhari says God reciprocates a servant's private remembrance privately and remembrance in an assembly in a better assembly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r3.anchor: وإن ذكرني في نفسه ذكرته في نفسي وإن ذكرني في ملإ ذكرته في ملإ خير منهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r4.claim: Remember God in solitude as you remember Him among people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r4.anchor: والمعنى : اذكر ربك وأنت في خلوتك كما تذكره في مجامع الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r5.claim: Dhikr here is verbal and includes Qur'an and other speech praising or thanking God, such as the testimony of faith, hawqala, tasbih, takbir, and supplication.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r5.anchor: والذكر حقيقة في ذكر اللسان ، وهو المراد هنا ، ويعضده قوله : { ودون الجهر من القول }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r6.claim: Tadarru means humility, which Arabs conventionally associate with raised speech; it alludes to raising the voice both literally and figuratively, as in 7:55.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p241/r6.anchor: و ( التضرع ) التذلل ولما كان التذلل يستلزم الخطاب بالصوت المرتفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r1.claim: Khifa is a verbal noun for fear; its morphological form is not meant to depict a particular posture or manner.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r1.anchor: وقوبل التضرع هنا بالخيفة وهي اسم مصدر الخوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r2.claim: Since fear is an inward reaction and makes one speak softly lest the feared one notice, khifa alludes here to quiet speech motivated by fear of God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r2.anchor: ولما كانت الخيفة انفعالا نفسيا يجده الإنسان في خاصة نفسه كانت مستلزمة للتخافت بالكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r3.claim: The pairing is an antithesis in both direct and allusive senses: humility with voicing and fear with secrecy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r3.anchor: فمقابلتها بالتضرع طباق في معنيي اللفظين الصريحين ومعنييهما الكناءين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r4.claim: The phrase denotes a middle volume, between loudness and secrecy; the verse thereby covers all modes of verbal remembrance, since people feel more energy for some than others.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r4.anchor: وهو الذكر المتوسط بين الجهر والإسرار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r5.claim: Ghudu is morning, the first half of the day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r5.anchor: اسم لزمن الصباح وهو النصف الأول من النهار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r6.claim: Asal is the plural of asil, meaning evening, the second half of the day until sunset.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r6.anchor: جمع أصيل وهو العشي وهو النصف الثاني من النهار إلى الغروب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r7.claim: The two terms cover the conventional span of daylight; night is generally for sleep, while waking hours receive special instruction such as 73:2 and also fall under the ban on heedlessness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r7.anchor: والمقصود استيعاب أجزاء النهار بحسب المتعارف ، فأما الليل فهو زمن النوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r8.claim: The warning concerns neglecting God's remembrance, but negligence has no fixed measure, since the Prophet's own circumstances include receiving revelation and ordinary needs such as eating.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r8.anchor: فدل قوله : { ولا تكن من الغافلين } على التحذير من الغفلة عن ذكر الله ولاحد للغفلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r9.claim: This command is specifically addressed to the Prophet; the community should emulate what is obligatory for him unless they are prohibited from it, as with continuous fasting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r9.anchor: وهذا الأمر خاص بالرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام ، وكل ما خص به الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r10.claim: Saying 'do not be among the heedless' is stronger than 'do not be heedless': it warns against joining a group characterized by heedlessness and makes the prohibited state clearer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p242/r10.anchor: وقد تقدم أن نحو { ولا تكن من الغافلين } أشد في الانتفاء وفي النهي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets remembrance as recitation in prayer, read silently in prayers where recitation is quiet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r1.anchor: أنه القراءة في الصلاة قاله ابن عباس فعلى هذا أمر أن يقرأ في نفسه في صلاة الإسرار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r2.claim: Qatāda interprets it as silently reciting behind the imam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r2.anchor: أنه القراءة خلف الإمام سرا في نفسه قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r3.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r3.claim: Al-Māwardī reports two further explanations: remembering God verbally and sustaining reflection so one does not become heedless of God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r3.anchor: أنه ذكر الله باللسان والرابع أنه ذكر الله باستدامة الفكر لا يغفل عن الله تعالى ذكر القولين الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the addressee to be the listener to the Qurʾān, whether in prayer or from a preacher.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r4.anchor: أحدهما أنه المستمع للقرآن إما في الصلاة وإما من الخطيب قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r5.claim: Another view makes the address to the Prophet, with its meaning applying generally to all morally responsible people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r5.anchor: والثاني أنه خطاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومعناه عام في جميع المكلفين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r6.claim: Tadarruʿ is humble submission, and khīfa is wariness of God’s punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p313/r6.anchor: التضرع الخشوع في تواضع والخيفة الحذر من عقابه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r1.claim: Jahr is making something public; a jahīr-voiced man has a loud voice. This wording indicates remembrance by the tongue, such as Qurʾān recitation or supplication, both recommended quietly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r1.anchor: الجهر الإعلان بالشيء ورجل جهير الصوت إذا كان صوته عاليا وفي هذا نص على أنه الذكر باللسان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r2.claim: The etiquette of loud prayer is clarified by 17:110, which commands neither excessively loud nor muted prayer recitation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r2.anchor: ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r3.claim: Al-ghuduww is the plural of ghudwa; al-āṣāl is the plural of aṣl, itself the plural of aṣīl, so it is a plural of a plural.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r3.anchor: فأما الغدو فهو جمع غدوة والآصال جمع أصل والأصل جمع أصيل فالآصال جمع الجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses al-āṣāl as the time from ʿaṣr until sunset and cites poetry using الأصائل.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة هي ما بين العصر إلى المغرب وأنشد لعمري لأنت البيت أكرم أهله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets al-ghuduww as the dawn prayer and al-āṣāl as the afternoon prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314/r5.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال يعني بالغدو صلاة الفجر والآصال صلاة العصر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r1.claim: Private remembrance broadly includes Qur'an recitation, supplication, glorification, the tahlīl, and other forms of dhikr.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r1.anchor: هو عام فى الأذكار من قراءة القرآن والدعاء والتسبيح والتهليل وغير ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ تضرعا وخيفة ﴾ متضرعا وخائفا ﴿ ودون الجهر من القول ﴾ متكلما كلاما دون الجهر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r3.claim: Speak below a loud voice, because quiet is more sincere and closer to sound reflection.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r3.anchor: لأن الاخافء ادخل فى الاخلاص واقرب إلى حسن التفكير

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r4.claim: Dawn and evening are specified for their merit; alternatively, the phrase calls for continual remembrance with steady reflection.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r4.anchor: لفضل هذين الوقتين وقيل المراد دامة الذكر باستقامة الفكر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r5.claim: Ghuduww means morning times; āṣāl is the plural of aṣl, itself a plural of aṣīl, the evening.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r5.anchor: بأوقات الغدو وهى الغدوات والآصال جمع أصل والأصل جمع أصيل وهو العشى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r6.claim: The heedless are those who neglect remembrance of God and become distracted from it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#4/r6.anchor: من الذين يغفلون عن ذكر الله ويلهون عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r1.claim: This parallels 7:55; al-Nahhas says inward remembrance means supplication.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r1.anchor:
ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية
[الأعراف: 55] وقد تقدم. قال أبو جعفر النحاس

QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says remembrance means recitation in prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r2.anchor: قلت: قد روي عن ابن عباس أنه يعني بالذكر القراءة في الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r3.claim: Another view is Quran recitation with reflection and contemplation.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r3.anchor: وقيل: المعنى اقرأ القرآن بتأمل وتدبر.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r4.claim: Taḍarruʿan is a verbal noun, possibly circumstantial; khīfatan is coordinated, and khīfah derives from khawf with wāw changed after kasra.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r4.anchor: «تضرعا» مصدر، وقد يكون في موضع الحال. «وخيفة» معطوف عليه. وجمع خيفة خوف

QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r5.claim: Speak below a loud voice, making yourself hear between loudness and whispering as in 17:110; Qurtubi says raising the voice in remembrance is forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r5.anchor: أي دون الرفع في القول. أي أسمع نفسك كما قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r6.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r6.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd say al-āṣāl means evenings; al-ghuduw is plural of ghudwah.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r6.anchor: قال قتادة وابن زيد: الآصال العشيات. والغدو جمع غدوة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r7.speaker: أبو مجلز
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r7.claim: Abu Mujliz reads بالغدو والإيصال, the verbal noun of entering the evening.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز «بالغدو والإيصال» وهو مصدر آصلنا، أي دخلنا في العشي.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r8.speaker: الزجاج والأخفش والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj, al-Akhfash, and al-Farra offer different plural analyses of āṣāl; al-Farra cites a poem using aṣl for the evening.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r8.anchor: والآصال جمع أصل مثل طنب وأطناب فهو جمع الجمع، والواحد أصيل، جمع على أصل عن الزجاج.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r9.speaker: الجوهري واللحياني
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r9.claim: Al-Jawhari defines aṣīl as after ʿAsr until sunset and lists plurals with poetry; he also gives aṣlān and aṣīlān, while al-Lihyani reports aṣīlālan.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r9.anchor: الجوهري: الأصيل الوقت بعد العصر إلى المغرب، وجمعه أصل وآصال وأصائل كأنه جمع أصيلة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r10.claim: Do not be heedless of remembrance.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:205/r10.anchor: { ولا تكن من الغافلين } أي عن الذكر

QASHANI:7:201-205/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:201-205/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:201-205/r8.claim: Remember God as present within yourself, following the cited example of the Messenger of God.

QASHANI:7:201-205/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:201-205/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:201-205/r9.claim: Humility in remembrance belongs to the station of differentiation within unity.
QASHANI:7:201-205/r9.anchor: في مقام التفصيل للجمع { وخيفة } في السر

QASHANI:7:201-205/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:201-205/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:201-205/r10.claim: Fear is inward fear of the self or fear that the self may claim a share in remembrance.
QASHANI:7:201-205/r10.anchor: في السر من النفس أو خيفة أن يكون للنفس فيه نصيب

QASHANI:7:201-205/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:201-205/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:201-205/r11.claim: The remembrance should not appear as the self’s public display; one should remember through God and for God, at dawn with spirit-light and at dusk under the self’s powers.
QASHANI:7:201-205/r11.anchor: أي: دون أن يظهر لك التضرع والذكر منك

QASHANI:7:201-205/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:201-205/r12.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:201-205/r12.claim: Do not be heedless at any time, especially when the self’s traits dominate; remain aware of essential unity.
QASHANI:7:201-205/r12.anchor: في حال من الأحوال، وخصوصا حال غلبات النفس وصفاتها

RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r1.claim: The preceding command to listen presupposes a loud Qur'an reciter, whom Rāzī identifies as the Prophet; after commanding him to proclaim revelation, God turns him to inward remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r1.anchor: ومعلوم أن ذلك القارىء ليس إلا الرسول عليه السلام ، فكانت هذه الآية جارية مجرى أمر الله

RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r2.claim: Remembrance in the prescribed inward, humble manner best completes its benefit because it is closer to sincerity and entreaty.
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r2.anchor: والفائدة فيه : أن انتفاع الإنسان بالذكر إنما يكمل إذا وقع الذكر بهذه الصفة ، لأنه بهذا الشرط أقرب إلى الأخلاص والتضرع

RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r3.claim: Remembering God inwardly means knowing the meanings of spoken invocations and bringing to mind His perfection, might, exaltedness, majesty, and greatness.
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r3.anchor: والمراد بذكر الله في نفسه كونه عارفا بمعاني الأذكار التي يقولها بلسانه

RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r4.claim: Verbal remembrance without awareness in the heart is fruitless, just as uttering 'I sold' or 'I bought' without understanding those words does not effect a sale.
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r4.anchor: الذكر باللسان إذا كان عاريا عن الذكر بالقلب كان عديم الفائدة

RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r5.claim: Rāzī recounts a spiritual master's method: after forty days of retreat and purification, the disciple hears the ninety-nine names and identifies which most moves the heart; steady repetition of that name may open disclosures.
RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r5.anchor: سمعت أن بعض الأكابر من أصحاب القلوب كان إذا أراد أن يأمر واحدا من المريدين بالخلوة والذكر

RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r1.speaker: المتكلمون
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r1.claim: The theologians argue that the command to remember God within oneself establishes inward speech, which they identify as inner remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r1.anchor: قال المتكلمون : هذه الآية تدل على إثبات كلام النفس

RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r2.claim: Rāzī rejects identifying this remembrance with knowledge: a present concept cannot be sought anew, while what is absent is inconceivable and cannot be sought; commanded inward remembrance must differ from knowledge and conception.
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r2.anchor: فثبت أنه لا قدرة للإنسان على تحصيل التصورات ، فامتنع ورود الأمر به ، والآية دالة على ورود الأمر بالذكر النفساني

RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r3.claim: Calling God 'your Lord' here, rather than using another divine name, signals care, nearness, favor, and beneficence, and should make the servant rejoice.
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r3.anchor: وإنما سماه في هذا المقام باسم كونه ربا ، وأضاف نفسه إليه

RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r4.claim: The name Lord recalls God's innumerable blessings, which human reason cannot encompass, as stated at 14:34; this recognition strengthens hope.
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r4.anchor: وعند سماع هذا الاسم يتذكر العبد أقسام نعم الله عليه

RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r5.claim: The Lord's name awakens hope and the command to beseech with fear awakens awe; together these motives complete faith, with hope given greater weight by the ordering.
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r5.anchor: فلما وقع الابتداء بما يوجب الرجاء ، علمنا أن جانب الرجاء أقوى

RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r6.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r6.claim: A Prophetic saying cited by Rāzī says that if a believer's fear and hope were weighed, they would balance one another.
RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r6.anchor: على ما قال عليه السلام : ( لو وزن خوف المؤمن ورجاؤه لاعتدلا )

RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r1.claim: Entreaty is an essential condition of remembrance, supported by the Qur'anic description of people calling on God in distress humbly and privately.
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r1.anchor: أما القرآن فقوله في سورة الأنعام { قل من ينجيكم من ظلمات البر والبحر تدعونه تضرعا وخفية }

RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r2.claim: Human completion requires awareness of divine lordship, expressed by inward remembrance, and witnessing one's servile lowliness, expressed by entreaty; movement between them resembles descent and ascent on a spiritual ascent.
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r2.anchor: كمال حال الإنسان إنما يحصل بانكشاف أمرين : أحدهما : عزة الربوبية ، وهذا المقصود

RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r3.claim: One answer to why these are separately commanded is that knowledge does not always entail humility and fear: someone may reason that God will not punish because punishment harms another without benefiting Him.
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r3.anchor: المعرفة لا يلزمها التضرع والخوف على الإطلاق

RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r4.claim: Another answer distinguishes fear of punishment, characteristic of beginners, from fear of divine majesty, characteristic of realized knowers and intensified by greater knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r4.anchor: وأجيب عنه بأن الخوف على قسمين : الأول : خوف العقاب ، وهو مقام المبتدين

RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r5.claim: A further answer says those granted unveilings experience both beauty and majesty: beauty sustains them, majesty overwhelms them, so remembrance must honor both aspects.
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r5.anchor: وأجيب عن هذا الجواب بأن لأصحاب المكاشفات مقامين : مكاشفة الجمال

RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r6.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r6.claim: An alternate reading has khafiyah; al-Zajjāj derives it from khawfah, with wāw changed to yāʾ because the preceding letter is kasra.
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r6.anchor: وفي قراءة أخرى { وخفية } وقال الزجاج : أصلها ( خوفة ) فقلبت الواو ياء لانكسار ما قبلها

RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r7.claim: Fear may be fear of shortcomings in one's deeds, fear of one's final outcome, or fear that deficient obedience and remembrance cannot repay God's limitless blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r7.anchor: أحدها : خوف التقصير في الأعمال . وثانيها : خوف الخاتمة . والمحققون خوفهم

RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r8.claim: The realized fear the prior divine decree, since what was settled beforehand only becomes apparent at the end.
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r8.anchor: والمحققون خوفهم من السابقة ، لأنه إنما يظهر في الخاتمة ما سبق الحكم به

RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r9.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r9.claim: The Prophetic saying 'the pen has dried concerning what will occur until Resurrection Day' supports fear of the prior decree.
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r9.anchor: ولذلك كان عليه السلام يقول : ( جف القلم بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة )

RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r10.speaker: أبو بكر الواسطي
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r10.claim: Abū Bakr al-Wāsiṭī says gratitude is shirk; Rāzī suggests he means that claiming to repay God's gifts with thanks makes the servant seem an independent giver, whereas humble gratitude reveals servitude.
RAZI-FULL:v15p87/r10.anchor: وكان الشيخ أبو بكر الواسطي يقول : الشكر شرك ، فسألوني عن هذه الكلمة

RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r1.claim: On the khafiyah reading, beginners conceal remembrance to protect worship from showing off, while the perfected conceal it out of the protective jealousy produced by complete love and absorption.
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r1.anchor: وأما القراءة الثانية : وهو قوله : { وخفية } فالإخفاء في حق المبتدين يراد لصون الطاعات

RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r2.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r2.claim: Rāzī supports the perfected person's hidden remembrance with a Prophetic saying that whoever knows God has his tongue fall silent.
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r2.anchor: بناء على قوله عليه السلام : ( من عرف الله كل لسانه )

RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r3.claim: Remembrance should be at a moderate volume between loudness and whispering, like the instruction for prayer at 17:110 and Zechariah's quiet call at 19:3.
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r3.anchor: والمراد منه أن يقع ذلك الذكر بحيث يكون متوسطا بين الجهر والمخافتة كما قال تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this means remembering the Lord at a volume one can hear oneself; vocal remembrance affects imagination and thereby strengthens inward spiritual remembrance in a reinforcing cycle.
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس : وتفسير قوله : { ودون الجهر من القول } المعنى أن يذكر ربه على وجه يسمع نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r5.claim: One analysis treats ghudū as the verbal noun of ghadā, later used for the time of morning departure, as in 'its morning course is a month' at 34:12.
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r5.anchor: أنه مصدر يقال غدوت أغدو غدوا غدوا ، ومنه قوله تعالى : { غدوها شهر } ( سبأ : 12 )

RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r6.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r6.claim: Al-Layth gives a second analysis: ghudū is the plural of ghudwah, meaning mornings.
