RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r6.anchor: قال الليث : الغدو جمع مثل الغدوات وواحد الغدوات غدوة

RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r7.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the singular of āṣāl is aṣl and the singular of aṣl is aṣīl; muʾṣilīn means arriving at the late-afternoon time.
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r7.anchor: فقال الفراء : واحدها أصل وواحد الأصل الأصيل . قال يقال جئناهم مؤصلين

RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r8.claim: Aṣīl is linked to aṣl, the beginning: the day with its night is treated as beginning at night, and day's end adjoins the next night's beginning.
RAZI-FULL:v15p88/r8.anchor: ويقال الأصيل مأخوذ من الأصل واليوم بليلته ، إنما يبتدأ بالشروع من أول الليل

RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r1.claim: Morning turns people from sleep like death to waking like life and the world from darkness to light; evening reverses the change. These striking transitions display God's wisdom and boundless power, warranting remembrance at both times.
RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r1.anchor: عند الغدوة انقلب الإنسان من النوم الذي هو كالموت إلى اليقظة التي هي كالحياة

RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r2.claim: Another view takes morning and evening to signify remembrance as continuously as possible; Ibn ʿAbbās says God would have commanded remembrance in any fourth human posture beyond standing, sitting, and lying down.
RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال في قوله : { الالباب الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم }

RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r3.claim: The two named times imply remembrance throughout all times, and the final command calls for constant inward awareness of God's majesty and greatness, without a moment of heedlessness insofar as human capacity allows.
RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r3.anchor: وقوله : { ولا تكن من الغافلين } يدل على أن الذكر القلبي يجب أن يكون دائما ، وأن لا يغفل الإنسان لحظة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r4.claim: Soul and body affect each other: imagining sourness makes the teeth ache and imagining an upsetting state heats the body, while repeated bodily action forms a strong, lasting disposition in the soul.
RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r4.anchor: لأن كل أثر حصل في جوهر الروح نزل منه أثر إلى البدن ، وكل حالة حصلت في البدن صعدت منها نتائج إلى الروح

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r1.claim: The command to remember the Lord is addressed to the Prophet but applies to everyone.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r1.anchor: The command to remember thy Lord is addressed to the Prophet, but applies to all people (R).

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r2.claim: The remembrance likely includes both verbal invocation of God and remembrance in the heart.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r2.anchor: It likely refers to both the invocation

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r3.claim: Remembrance may take the form of Quran recitation, praise and glorification, or the testimony to God's Oneness.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r3.anchor: This “remembrance” may also take the form of reciting the Quran or uttering words of praise and glorification for God

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r4.claim: Read after the previous verse, the command may mean remembering God while hearing Quran recitation.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r4.anchor: Read in connection with the previous verse, remember thy Lord may be an injunction to remember God when one hears the Quran

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r5.claim: Remembering God within one's soul can also mean remembering Him within oneself.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r5.anchor: To remember God within thy soul may also mean to remember Him “within thyself,”

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r6.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī connects the verse to a sacred hadith: when a servant remembers God privately or in an assembly, God remembers him correspondingly, in a nobler assembly in the latter case.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r6.anchor: al-Ṭabarīconnects this verse with a famous

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r7.claim: The verse is a major basis for dhikr, especially in Sufism, as a means of unveiling and deeper understanding of God.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r7.anchor: The present verse is one of the most important in suggesting the spiritual importance of dhikr (remembrance or invocation)

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r8.claim: Dhikr allows recognition that God is near and witnesses one's thoughts and deeds, and can lead to experiencing His Presence.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r8.anchor: as a means of experiencing His Presence and one’s immersion “in the ocean of Divinity.”

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r9.speaker: a ḥadīth
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r9.claim: A hadith says everything on earth is accursed except remembrance of God.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r9.anchor: According to a ḥadīth, “All that is on the earth is accursed save the remembrance of God.”

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r10.claim: Humble, quiet remembrance resembles commands to supplicate humbly and secretly and guides Sufi dhikr practice.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r10.anchor: The command to remember God humbly and in awe, being not loud of voice, is similar to the command to call upon Him humbly and in secret

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r11.claim: Lowering the voice is also enjoined in supplication, speech before the Prophet, and general conduct; the Quran likens the vilest voices to donkeys.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r11.anchor: Lowering one’s voice is also enjoined during supplicatory prayer (17:110), when speaking in the presence of the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r12.claim: Quiet prayer signals sincerity rather than seeking to be seen and helps reflection and recollection.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r12.anchor: To pray quietly reflects sincerity in one’s prayer (Aj, R, Z), indicating that one is not praying to be seen of men

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r13.speaker: the Companions
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r13.claim: When Companions asked whether God was near enough for whispers or far enough to require shouts, 2:186 was revealed affirming His nearness and response to callers.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r13.anchor: The Prophet was once asked by some Companions whether God was near, so that they should whisper to Him, or far away, so that they should shout

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r14.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r14.claim: Al-Rāzī says invocation should be audible to oneself, not wholly silent: bodily hearing stirs imagination and soul, strengthening the spiritual heart as body, soul, and spirit reinforce one another.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r14.anchor: Al-Rāzī explains that the invocation or remembrance enjoined here should be done not silently, but in a voice low enough that it can be heard only by oneself

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r15.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r15.claim: The quiet-voice command might be taken to prohibit loud communal Sufi dhikr.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r15.anchor: some might consider this verse as prohibiting the loud, communal dhikr practiced by Sufi groups.

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r16.speaker: Ibn ʿAjībah
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAjībah rejects using the verse to ban loud communal dhikr: it was revealed in Mecca amid circumspect worship, while the Prophet and Companions later held public mosque dhikr in Medina.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r16.anchor: Ibn ʿAjībah, however, rejects this interpretation, noting that this verse was revealed in Makkah, when the believers had to be circumspect

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r17.claim: Morning and evening are especially suited times for remembrance, supplication, and praise; they may also represent remembrance at all times.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r17.anchor: The morning and the evening are mentioned here and elsewhere as times particularly suited to remembering, supplicating, or praising God

STUDYQURAN:7:205/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r18.claim: Morning and evening symbolize transitions between light and dark and sleep and waking, suggesting death and resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:7:205/r18.anchor: each being a time of transition between light and darkness, sleeping and waking, and thus suggestive of death and resurrection (Aj, R).

SULAMI:v1p252#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p252#4/r1.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p252#4/r1.claim: Do not publicize remembrance to yourself in search of recompense; the finest remembrance is witnessed only by God, and hidden remembrance is superior to outward remembrance.
SULAMI:v1p252#4/r1.anchor: قال الحسين في هذه الآية : لا يظهر ذكرك لنفسك فتطلب به عوضا ، فأشرف الذكر ما لا يشرف عليه إلا الحق

SULAMI:v1p252#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p252#4/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p252#4/r2.claim: Whoever loses even one breath without remembering God is heedless.
SULAMI:v1p252#4/r2.anchor: قال سهل : حقا أقول لكم لا باطلا يقينا لا شك ما من أحد ذهب عنه نفس واحد بغير ذكر الله إلا وهو غافل

SULAMI:v1p252#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p252#4/r3.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p252#4/r3.claim: A heedless person is one who fails to grasp the realities of things.
SULAMI:v1p252#4/r3.anchor: وقال : الغافل من غفل عن درك حقائق الأمور

TAB-FULL:v10p663/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says remembrance in 7:205 is for obligatory prayer and later stories or recitation are supererogatory; he reports that companions recited behind the Prophet in an obligatory prayer, confusing him, after which 7:204 was revealed for that prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أنه كان يقول في هذه: " {واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة} [الأعراف: 205] هذا في المكتوبة

TAB-FULL:v10p668/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r1.claim: The listener should take heed from Quranic verses, reflect on them, and remember returning to God when hearing the Quran in prayer or a sermon.
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r1.anchor: اتعظ بما في آي القرآن، واعتبر به، وتذكر معادك إليه عند سماعكه

TAB-FULL:v10p668/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r2.claim: Remembering God with humility means acting humbly and submissively toward Him.
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r2.anchor: افعل ذلك تخشعا لله وتواضعا له

TAB-FULL:v10p668/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r3.claim: Fear God lest He punish you for failing to heed and reflect, or neglecting the limits He has set.
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r3.anchor: وخوفا من الله أن يعاقبك على تقصير يكون منك في الاتعاظ به والاعتبار

TAB-FULL:v10p668/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r4.claim: The remembrance is supplication to God in a quiet voice rather than aloud.
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r4.anchor: ودعاء باللسان لله في خفاء لا جهار

TAB-FULL:v10p668/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says not to make this remembrance audible.
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة ودون الجهر من القول} [الأعراف: 205] لا يجهر بذلك

TAB-FULL:v10p668/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r6.claim: Mujahid says people were commanded to remember God in their hearts with humility and fear.
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r6.anchor: سمعت مجاهدا، يقول في قوله: " {واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة ودون الجهر من القول} [الأعراف: 205] الآية، قال: أمروا

TAB-FULL:v10p668/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r7.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r7.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr transmits God's saying that He remembers a servant who remembers Him privately in kind, and remembers one who mentions Him among people in a better and nobler company.
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r7.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير، في قوله: " {واذكر ربك في نفسك} [الأعراف: 205] قال: «يقول الله إذا ذكرني عبدي في نفسه

TAB-FULL:v10p668/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj says supplication should be humble and subdued; raising the voice, calling out, and shouting in prayer are disliked.
TAB-FULL:v10p668/r8.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: " {واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة} [الأعراف: 205] قال: يؤمر بالتضرع في الدعاء والاستكانة

TAB-FULL:v10p669/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r1.claim: The phrase means in the mornings and evenings.
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {بالغدو والآصال} [الأعراف: 205] قال: بالبكر والعشي

TAB-FULL:v10p669/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r2.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r2.claim: Some Arabic grammarians say al-asal is the plural of asil, by analogy with al-ayman as the plural of yamin and al-asrar as the plural of sarir.
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r2.anchor: وهذا القول أولى بالصواب في ذلك، وهو أنه جائز أن يكون جمع أصيل وأصل لأنهما قد يجمعان على أفعال

TAB-FULL:v10p669/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r3.speaker: آخرون من أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r3.claim: Other grammarians say it is the plural of asl, which is itself the plural of asil.
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r3.anchor: وهذا القول أولى بالصواب في ذلك، وهو أنه جائز أن يكون جمع أصيل وأصل لأنهما قد يجمعان على أفعال

TAB-FULL:v10p669/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r4.speaker: آخرون من أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r4.claim: Other grammarians say al-asal is a plural of both asl and asil.
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r4.anchor: وهذا القول أولى بالصواب في ذلك، وهو أنه جائز أن يكون جمع أصيل وأصل لأنهما قد يجمعان على أفعال

TAB-FULL:v10p669/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r5.claim: Tabari prefers allowing al-asal to be a plural of either asil or asl, since both forms can take the plural pattern afʿal.
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r5.anchor: وهذا القول أولى بالصواب في ذلك، وهو أنه جائز أن يكون جمع أصيل وأصل لأنهما قد يجمعان على أفعال

TAB-FULL:v10p669/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r6.claim: In Arab usage, al-asal denotes the period from the afternoon prayer time until sunset.
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r6.anchor: وأما الآصال فهي فيما يقال في كلام العرب ما بين العصر إلى المغرب

TAB-FULL:v10p669/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r7.claim: Do not be distracted from Quranic admonitions, lessons, and wonders; instead reflect and understand them, keeping God's remembrance, submission, and fear in your heart.
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r7.anchor: ولكن تدبر ذلك وتفهمه، وأشعره قلبك بذكر الله وخضوع له وخوف من قدرة الله عليك

TAB-FULL:v10p669/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the phrase as morning and afternoon.
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {بالغدو والآصال} [الأعراف: 205] قال: بالبكر والعشي

TAB-FULL:v10p669/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r9.speaker: أبو وائل
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r9.claim: Abu Wa'il's question to his servant at sunset uses asal to mean that evening time has arrived.
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r9.anchor: قال: سمعت أبا وائل، يقول لغلامه عند مغيب الشمس: «آصلنا بعد؟»

TAB-FULL:v10p669/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r10.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r10.claim: Mujahid identifies ghuduw with the end of dawn at the morning prayer and asal with the end of evening at the afternoon prayer; he also explains 3:41's evening and early morning as the period from the sun's decline to sunset and the start of dawn.
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r10.anchor: قال مجاهد، قوله: " {بالغدو والآصال} [الأعراف: 205] قال: الغدو: آخر الفجر صلاة الصبح، والآصال: آخر العشي صلاة العصر

TAB-FULL:v10p669/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r11.claim: When asked about the dawn prayer, Ibn Abbas says it is in God's Book but people do not uphold it, then recites 24:36.
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس، سئل عن صلاة الفجر، فقال: " إنها لفي كتاب الله، ولا يقوم عليها، ثم قرأ: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36]

TAB-FULL:v10p669/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r12.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r12.claim: Qatada says God commands remembrance and forbids heedlessness; ghuduw is the dawn prayer and asal is the evening.
TAB-FULL:v10p669/r12.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة} [الأعراف: 205] إلى قوله: {بالغدو والآصال} [الأعراف: 205] أمر الله بذكره، ونهى عن الغفلة

TUSTARI:7:205/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:205/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:205/r1.claim: True remembrance is certain knowledge that God sees you, inward awareness of His nearness, modesty before Him, and choosing Him over yourself in every circumstance; merely claiming remembrance does not make one a rememberer.
TUSTARI:7:205/r1.anchor: تحقيق العلم بأن الله تعالى مشاهدك

TUSTARI:7:205/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:205/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:7:205/r2.claim: In the saying that the world and its contents are accursed except God's remembrance, Sahl glosses remembrance as avoiding a forbidden act when one recalls that God is watching.

TUSTARI:7:205/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:205/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:205/r3.claim: Sahl insists that anyone who spends even one breath outside remembrance is heedless of God.
TUSTARI:7:205/r3.anchor: ما من أحد ذهب منه نفس واحد في غير ذكر الله إلا وهو غافل عن الله عز وجل

TUSTARI:7:205/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:205/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:205/r4.claim: The elite's heedlessness is settling into a thing; the ordinary person's is taking pride in it.
TUSTARI:7:205/r4.anchor: غفلة الخاص السكون إلى الشيء، وغفلة العام

TABRISI:7:204-205/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:204-205/r3.claim: Āṣāl is a plural of aṣīl and itself a plural-of-plural; it means evenings, from afternoon until sunset.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r3.anchor: والآصال جمع أصل وأصل جمع أصيل فالآصال جمع الجمع وتصغيره أصيلان

TABRISI:7:204-205/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:204-205/r4.claim: Taḍarruʿan and khīfatan are circumstantial accusatives; dūna al-jahr is coordinated and means without raising the voice to loudness.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r4.anchor: تضرعا وخيفة مصدران وضعا موضع الحال أي متضرعين وخائفين ودون الجهر عطف عليه

TABRISI:7:204-205/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:204-205/r16.claim: The address is to the Prophet, but its intended audience is general.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r16.anchor: خطاب للنبي عليه وآله السلام والمراد به عام

TABRISI:7:204-205/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r17.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:7:204-205/r17.claim: Another view addresses the Qurʾān's listener: remember God inwardly through glorification, profession of unity, and praise.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r17.anchor: وقيل: هو خطاب لمستمع القرآن والمعنى واذكر ربك في نفسك بالكلام

TABRISI:7:204-205/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r18.speaker: أحدهما
TABRISI:7:204-205/r18.claim: Zurāra reports from one of the two Imams: behind an imam, listen and glorify God inwardly when he does not recite aloud.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r18.anchor: روى زرارة عن أحدهما ع قال معناه إذا كنت خلف الإمام تأتم به فانصت وسبح في نفسك

THALABI:v4p322/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p322/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p322/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets remembrance as Quran recitation in prayer, with supplication aloud and fear privately; دون الجهر means a subdued voice.
THALABI:v4p322/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني بالذكر القراءة في الصلاة تضرعا جهرا وخيفة ودون الجهر دون رفع القول في خفض وسكوت

THALABI:v4p322/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p322/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v4p322/r5.claim: The people of meanings explain remembrance as taking admonition from the Quran, believing its signs, and obeying its commands in humility and fear of punishment.
THALABI:v4p322/r5.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: واذكر ربك اتعظ بالقرآن وآمن بآياته واذكر ربك بالطاعة في ما يأمرك

THALABI:v4p322/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p322/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v4p322/r6.claim: When reciting, one should call upon God quietly rather than aloud.
THALABI:v4p322/r6.anchor: فإذا قرأت دعوت بالله أي دون الجهر: خفاء لا جهار

THALABI:v4p322/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p322/r7.speaker: مجاهد وابن جريج
THALABI:v4p322/r7.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj say the command is to remember God in one's heart and to supplicate humbly and submissively.
THALABI:v4p322/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد وابن جريج: أمر أن يذكروه في الصدور. ويؤمر بالتضرع في الدعاء والاستكانة

THALABI:v4p322/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p322/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p322/r8.claim: The source says raising one's voice and beginning supplication are disliked.

THALABI:v4p322/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p322/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p322/r9.claim: Al-ghuduw and al-asal mean mornings and evenings; asil is the singular of asal, the interval from afternoon until sunset.
THALABI:v4p322/r9.anchor: فإنه يعني بالبكر والعشيات، واحد الآصال أصيل، مثل أيمان ويمين، وقال أهل اللغة: هو ما بين العصر إلى المغرب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r1.claim: The address is to the Prophet, but the instruction also applies generally to all legally responsible people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r1.anchor: الخطاب في هذا للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وغيره داخل فيه لأنه عام لسائر المكلفين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets remembrance here as recitation in prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يعني بالذكر القراءة في الصلاة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as entreating God and fearing Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r3.anchor: {تضرعا وخيفة} قال: (يريد: يتضرع إلي ويخاف مني)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r4.claim: The phrase means humble submission to God and fear of His punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r4.anchor: ومعناه: (¬1) استكانة لي وخوفا من عذابي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives khīfah from khawfah, with wāw changed to yāʾ because the preceding consonant is kasra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: (أصلها خوفة. فقلبت الواو ياء لانكسار ما قبلها)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r6.claim: Dūna al-jahr means below loudness, and min al-qawl refers to Quran.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r6.anchor: {ودون الجهر} دون الرفع {من القول} من القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r7.claim: Al-ghuduw and al-āsāl mean morning and evening and, in this interpretation, refer to the prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r7.anchor: فعلى (¬5) هذا القول الآية وردت في القراءة في الصلوات كلها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r8.claim: On the prayer interpretation, the verse covers all prayers: recite quietly in silent prayers and moderately in audible prayers, following the instruction to seek a middle course.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r8.anchor: فعلى (¬5) هذا القول الآية وردت في القراءة في الصلوات كلها لقوله تعالى: {يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r9.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r9.claim: Qatada says God commanded remembrance and forbade heedlessness, identifying dawn with Fajr and evening with Asr; this limits the verse to those two prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة (¬2): (أمر الله بذكره ونهى عن الغفلة، أما {بالغدو} فصلاة الصبح، وأما بالعشي فصلاة العصر)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r10.speaker: مجاهد وابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r10.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj say remembrance is inward, with humility and submission, and raised voices and calling out in supplication are disliked.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد (¬3) وابن جريج (¬4): (أمر أن تذكروه في الصدور بالتضرع والاستكانة، ويكره رفع الصوت والنداء بالدعاء)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r11.claim: On Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj's view, the verse concerns inward remembrance and avoiding shouts in supplication.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p570/r11.anchor: وعلى هذا الآية وردت في ذكر الله تعالى بالقلب، وترك الصياح في الدعاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r1.claim: Al-ghuduw is a verbal noun of ghada, but may also name the time of morning departure; it may alternatively be a plural of ghudwah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r1.anchor: الغدو مصدر، يقال: غدوت أغدو (¬6) غدوا وغدوا ومنه قوله: {غدوها شهر} [سبأ: 12] أي: غدوها للسير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r2.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r2.claim: Al-Layth says al-ghuduw is a plural like al-ghadawat, whose singular is ghudwah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r2.anchor: قال الليث: (الغدو جمع مثل الغدوات وواحد الغدوات غدوة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r3.speaker: الراجز
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r3.claim: The cited rajaz line uses غدوة as a singular form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r3.anchor: قال الراجز (¬2): جرت عليه كل ريح ريدة ... هو جاء سفواء نؤوج الغدوة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r4.claim: Al-Farra says the singular of āṣāl is aṣl, and the singular of aṣl is aṣīl; مؤصلين means arriving at evening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: (واحدها أصل، وواحد الأصل أصيل.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj calls al-āsāl evenings, a plural of a plural.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r6.speaker: النابغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r6.claim: Al-Nabigha's line uses aṣīlan to mean evening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r6.anchor: ومنه قول النابغة (¬1): وقفت فيها أصيلا كي (¬2) أسائلها أي: عشية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r7.claim: Aṣīl may derive from aṣl, the bottom of a thing: late afternoon is where the day descends toward its end, hence its name.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p572/r7.anchor: ويقال: الأصيل (¬3) مأخوذ من الأصل وهو أسفل كل شيء، وما بعد العصر ينتهي إليه النهار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r7.claim: Remembering God inwardly means reciting in prayer humbly and fearfully, without raising the voice.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r7.anchor: { واذكر ربك في نفسك } يعني: القراءة في الصلاة { تضرعا وخيفة } استكانة لي وخوفا من عذابي { ودون الجهر } دون الرفع

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r8.claim: The command covers silent recitation in quiet prayers and lowered voice in aloud prayers at morning and evening.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r8.anchor: { من القول بالغدو والآصال } بالبكر والعشيات. أمر أن يقرأ في نفسه في صلاة الإسرار، ودون الجهر فيما يرفع به الصوت

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r9.claim: The heedless are those who do not recite in their prayers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r9.anchor: { ولا تكن من الغافلين } الذين لا يقرؤون في صلاتهم.

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r19.claim: Remember God inwardly and verbally with supplication and fear; use a voice below public loudness but audible to oneself, in words of recitation, prayer, or other remembrance that do not obstruct thought.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r19.anchor: bir tazarru‘suretiyle ve bir nevi havf ile yalvararak ve korkarak kalben ve fikren

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r20.claim: Make inward remembrance a regular practice morning and evening, keeping the heart awake and constantly remembering God rather than among the heedless.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r20.anchor: Kalbin dâima uyanık ve zikrullahda dâim olsun

ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r1.claim: The unusual bond between soul and body displays heart-consciousness and the unity of the self; through it a moment of awareness of God's oneness dawns.
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r1.anchor: Nefs-i insânîde rûh ile bedenin pek acîb bir alâkası vardır ki vicdân-ı kalb ve vahdet-i nefsiye bu alâkada tecellî eder

ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r2.claim: Effects in the soul can descend into the body: imagining sourness makes the teeth ache, while imagining tragedy can cause headache, heat, or fainting.
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r2.anchor: en âdî bir misâl olmak üzere bir ekşi tahayyülünden diş kamaşır ve bir fâcia tahayyülünden baş ağrısı, harâret veya baygınlık hâsıl olur

ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r3.claim: The reverse also occurs: repeating bodily acts forms a strong disposition in the soul.
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r3.anchor: bu da bedenden rûha çıkan âsârdır

ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r4.claim: When spoken remembrance is audible to oneself without hindering thought, it creates an image in imagination; light rises to the soul and reflects through soul, tongue, imagination, and intellect, mutually strengthening them.
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r4.anchor: bu zikr-i lisânîden hayâlde bir eser husûle gelir. Ve bundan rûha bir nûr yükselir, sonra bu envâr rûhtan lisâna, lisândan hayâle, hayâlden akla in‘ikas eder

ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r5.claim: The stages of this ascent have no limit; the journey of knowing seeks God through the endless sea, with the self as its ship and remembrance as its rudder.
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r5.anchor: Sefer-i ma‘rifet işte bu nihâyetsiz deryâda matlûb-ı Hakk’a yürümektir. Bu seyrin yegâne gemisi nefis ve yegâne dümeni zikrullahtır

ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r6.claim: Complete heedlessness is a grave danger, and even a moment of heedlessness may be perilous.
ELMALILI:7:200-205#2/r6.anchor: Gaflet-i külliye hatar-ı mutlak ve her gaflet lahzası bile bir hatar-ı muhtemildir

MAJAZ:v1p238/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p238/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p238/r1.claim: Khīfatan means fear; the wāw drops from its form because of the kasra on khāʾ.
MAJAZ:v1p238/r1.anchor: تضرعا وخيفة» (204) أي خوفا وذهبت الواو بكسرة الخاء.

MAJAZ:v1p238/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p238/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p238/r2.claim: Āṣāl is plural of aṣl, whose singular is aṣīl; it denotes the time between afternoon and sunset, supported by Abū Dhuʾayb’s aṣāʾil.
MAJAZ:v1p238/r2.anchor: والآصال» (204) واحدتها أصل وواحد الأصل أصيل ومجازه: ما بين العصر إلى المغرب، وقال [أبو ذؤيب]

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r1.claim: Dhikr literally means remembering or keeping something in mind, with the heart or tongue.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r1.anchor: Sözlükte “bir şeyi kalple veya dil ile anma, hatırlama, akılda tutma” anlamına gelen zikir kelimesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r2.claim: As a religious term, dhikr means remembering and invoking God, keeping Him present in heart and speech, and avoiding heedlessness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r2.anchor: dinî bir terim olarak “Allah’ı anmak, hatırlamak, dilde ve gönülde tutmak, O’nu unutmamak, gaflet halinde olmamak” mânasında kullanılır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r3.claim: More specifically, dhikr can mean repeating God’s name, the Beautiful Names, or other devotional formulas such as la ilaha illa Allah.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r3.anchor: daha özel olarak Allah ismini ve esmâ-i hüsnâyı, “lâ ilâhe illallah” gibi diğer dinî ifade kalıplarını dilde tekrar etmeye de zikir denir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r4.claim: Sufi orders also call the regular repetition of divine names and other devotional phrases at set times and counts dhikr.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r4.anchor: Tarikat ehlinin Allah’ın isimleriyle dinî mahiyetteki başka bazı kelime ve ibareleri belli zamanlarda ve belli sayılarda düzenli olarak dilde tekrar etmeleri de zikir kelimesiyle ifade edilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r5.claim: In Quran 13:28 and 24:37 and in hadith, dhikr usually means keeping God’s name on the tongue and awareness of Him alive in the mind without fixing a time or count.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r5.anchor: zikir, genellikle herhangi bir zaman veya sayı belirlemeksizin, müminin dilinde Allah ismini ve zihninde Allah bilincini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r6.claim: This verse calls for inward as well as verbal remembrance, with a servant’s reverence, humility, and supplication that trembles in awe of God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r6.anchor: Konumuz olan âyette Allah’ı dil ile zikrederken aynı zamanda ruhen de zikir halinde olmak, kulluk şuuru ve edebiyle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r7.speaker: Gazzâlî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r7.claim: Al-Ghazali calls dhikr the highest and most beneficial worship, but says it requires intimacy with God and love in the heart; tongue-only repetition without that state does not improve spiritual or moral life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r7.anchor: Gazzâlî (İhyâ’, I, 293-304), zikrin bütün ibadetlerin en yücesi ve en faydalısı olduğunu, fakat bu özelliği taşıyabilmesi için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r8.claim: The closing warning against heedlessness underscores that dhikr should involve inward awareness rather than remain on the tongue alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:205/r8.anchor: Nitekim âyetin sonundaki “Gafillerden olma!” uyarısı da bu hususa işaret etmektedir.

BURHAN:v2p137/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p137/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p137/r6.claim: The instruction to remember God inwardly and without loud speech supports keeping the two testimonies quiet in the call to prayer.
BURHAN:v2p137/r6.anchor: وأما إسراره بهما يعنى بالشهادتين فمن مفهوم قوله

NAHHAS:v2p171/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p171/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p171/r12.claim: Taḍarruʿan is a verbal noun and may be circumstantial; khīfatan is singular, while khawf is collective with the same meaning, and al-Farrāʾ also records khīf.
NAHHAS:v2p171/r12.anchor: مصدر وقد يكون في موضع الحال وجمع خيفة خوف لأنها بمعنى الخوف وحكى الفراء أنه يقال أيضا خيف

NAHHAS:v2p171/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p171/r13.speaker: أبو مجلز
NAHHAS:v2p171/r13.claim: Abū Mujliz reads bil-ghuduwwi wa-l-īṣāl, with īṣāl a verbal noun meaning entering the evening.
NAHHAS:v2p171/r13.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز ( بالغدو والإيصال ) وهو مصدر أصلنا أي دخلنا في العشي

NAHHAS:v2p171/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p171/r14.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p171/r14.claim: Al-Akhfash says al-āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, like yamīn/aymān; al-Farrāʾ says aṣul is its plural and may also be singular.

ITQAN:v1p188#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r1.claim: Knowing verse counts and endings has legal consequences, including rules for prayer, sermons, night worship, and stopping.
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r1.anchor: يترتب على معرفة الآي وعدها وفواصلها أحكام فقهية منها اعتبارها فيمن جهل الفاتحة فإنه يجب عليه بدلها سبع آيات

ITQAN:v1p188#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r3.claim: A sermon must include a complete verse; whether a disputed verse ending suffices is uncertain, and the author has found no one who discusses it.
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r3.anchor: ومنها اعتبارها في الخطبة فإنه يجب فيها قراءة آية كاملة ولا يكفي شطرها إن لم تكن طويلة

ITQAN:v1p188#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r4.claim: A sound report says the Prophet recited sixty to one hundred verses in the dawn prayer.
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r4.anchor: ومنها اعتبارها في السورة التي تقرأ في الصلاة أو ما يقوم مقامها ففي الصحيح أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ في الصبح بالستين إلى المائة

ITQAN:v1p188#3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r5.claim: Reports give escalating night-recitation rewards at 10, 50, 100, 200, and 300 verses, with further versions at 500, 700, and 1,000, collected by al-Darimi.
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r5.anchor: ومنها اعتبارها في قراءة قيام الليل ففي أحاديث من قرأ بعشر آيات لم يكتب من الغافلين ومن قرأ بخمسين آية

ITQAN:v1p188#3/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r6.claim: Verse counting also matters for where the reciter stops.
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r6.anchor: ومنها اعتبارها في الوقف عليها كما سيأتي

ITQAN:v1p188#3/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r7.speaker: الزعفراني
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r7.claim: Al-Zafarani dismisses verse counting as no real knowledge, alleging some used it to drum up business.
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r7.anchor: حتى قال الزعفراني العدد ليس بعلم وإنما اشتغل به بعضهم ليروج به سوقه

ITQAN:v1p188#3/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r8.speaker: الهذلي
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r8.claim: Al-Hudhali rejects that dismissal: counting identifies stopping places; scholars differ whether prayer is valid with one, three, or seven verses, while half a verse is insufficient by consensus.
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r8.anchor: وقال الهذلي في كامله أعلم أن قوما جهلوا العدد وما فيه من الفوائد حتى قال الزعفراني العدد ليس بعلم

ITQAN:v1p188#3/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r9.speaker: الهذلي
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r9.claim: Al-Hudhali adds that Quranic inimitability does not occur below a complete verse, another reason verse counts matter.
ITQAN:v1p188#3/r9.anchor: والإعجاز لا يقع بدون آية فللعدد فائدة عظيمة في ذلك انتهى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p155/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p155/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p155/r1.claim: The comparison to a startled or released crow conveys swift, extended flight: fear or sudden freedom drives it farther than an unhurried bird flying by choice.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p155/r1.anchor: نظير غرابا ولم يقل غراب يطير مثلا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p155/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p155/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p155/r2.claim: Ibn Fāris compares a hawk’s beak only to the curved upper stroke of a left-handed jim; the later letters clarify that the dots and lower stroke are excluded.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p155/r2.anchor: أراد أن يشبه المنقار بالجيم والجيم خطان الأول الذي مبدأه وهو الأعلى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p155/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p155/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p155/r3.claim: The follow-up explicitly narrows the comparison to the jim’s first stroke, and the poet’s mention of thought signals the care needed for such precision.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p155/r3.anchor: فأراك عيانا أنه عمد في التشبيه إلى الخط الأول من الجيم دون تعريقها ودون الخط الأسفل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r1.claim: A finite verb conveys an action unfolding repeatedly, whereas a participial adjective presents a settled quality: the fire keeps blazing, and the ʿarif keeps scrutinizing faces in turn.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r1.anchor: هناك موقدا يتجدد منه الإلهاب والإشعال حالا فحالا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r2.claim: In the question about provision, the Qur'an's verb يرزقكم conveys an action; replacing it with the participle رازق لكم would alter the intended meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r2.anchor: هل من خالق غير الله يرزقكم من السماء والأرض

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r3.claim: Although زيد يقوم may occupy the same predicate position as زيد قائم, a verb and a noun are not semantically interchangeable because their grammatical forms differ.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r3.anchor: لم يكن أحدهما فعلا والآخر اسما

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r4.claim: زيد منطلق reports a departure to someone unaware that it occurred; زيد المنطلق identifies Zayd as the agent of an already known departure, while المنطلق زيد also has its own distinct purpose.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p142/r4.anchor: كان كلامك مع من لم يعلم أن انطلاقا كان لا من زيد ولا من عمرو

TABATABAI:7:205-206/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r2.claim: The verse commands inward remembrance and quiet spoken remembrance; loud remembrance is passed over because it conflicts with the etiquette of servitude, not because it is not remembrance.
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r2.anchor: قسم الذكر إلى ما في النفس ودون الجهر من القول ثم أمر بالقسمين

TABATABAI:7:205-206/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r3.claim: During a night march through a frightening valley, companions called takbir loudly; the Prophet stopped them, saying they were not calling someone absent and far away.
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r3.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سار بأصحابه في بعض غزواته فدخلوا واديا موحشا والليل داج فكان ينادي بعض أصحابه بالتكبير فنهاه النبي

TABATABAI:7:205-206/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r4.claim: Tadarruʿ derives from ḍarāʿa and means entreating with humility; khīfa is a form of fear suited to God’s sanctity.
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r4.anchor: والتضرع من الضراعة وهو التملق بنوع من الخشوع والخضوع، والخيفة بناء نوع من الخوف

TABATABAI:7:205-206/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r5.claim: Remembrance combines attraction toward God through love and desire with retreat through awe; His beautiful names attract creation, while His majestic names overpower and repel it.
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r5.anchor: ففي التضرع معنى الميل إلى المتضرع إليه والرغبة فيه والتقرب منه، وفي الخيفة معنى اتقائه والرهبة والتبعد عنه

TABATABAI:7:205-206/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r6.claim: Morning and evening grammatically qualify quiet spoken remembrance, distributing it across those times and aligning it with some daily obligatory prayers.
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r6.anchor: وقوله { بالغدو والآصال } ، ظاهرة أنه قيد لقوله { ودون الجهر من القول } فيكون الذكر القولي

TABATABAI:7:205-206/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r7.claim: The prohibition is against joining the settled class of the heedless, not against every momentary lapse; one should resume remembrance and prevent heedlessness from taking root.
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r7.anchor: ولم ينه تعالى عن أصل الغفلة، وإنما نهى عن الدخول في زمرة الغافلين، وهم الموصوفون بالغفلة الذين استقرت فيهم هذه الصفة

TABATABAI:7:205-206/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r8.claim: The verse’s overall command is to remember God inwardly with humility and awe at intervals, and to remember Him quietly aloud morning and evening.
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r8.anchor: فمحصل الآية الأمر بالاستمرار على ذكر الله في النفس تضرعا وخيفة حينا بعد حين، وذكره بالقول دون الجهر بالغدو والآصال

TABRISI:7:205-206/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:205-206/r1.claim: One explanation is to remember God's blessing by reflecting on oneself; another is to remember Him inwardly through His exalted attributes and beautiful names.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r1.anchor: وقيل: أراد ذكره في نفسك بصفاته العليا وأسمائه الحسنى

TABRISI:7:205-206/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:205-206/r2.claim: Remember God in supplication with humility and fear, qualities that make prayer more likely to be answered; remembering inwardly is farther from showing off, according to al-Jubba'i.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r2.anchor: يعني بتضرع وخوف يعني في الدعاء فإن الدعاء بالتضرع والخوف من الله تعالى أقرب إلى الإجابة

TABRISI:7:205-206/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:205-206/r3.claim: Raise the voice somewhat without shouting excessively, keeping a moderate level between loudness and silence.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r3.anchor: أرفعوا أصواتكم قليلا ولا تجهروا بها جهارا بليغا حتى يكون عدلا بين ذلك

TABRISI:7:205-206/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:7:205-206/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the instruction as telling the prayer leader to recite loudly enough for those behind him to hear.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r4.anchor: إنه أمر للإمام أن يرفع صوته في الصلاة بالقراءة مقدار ما يسمع من خلفه عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:7:205-206/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r5.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:7:205-206/r5.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as mornings and evenings; these periods stand for keeping remembrance continuous.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r5.anchor: أي بالغدوات والعشيات عن قتادة والمراد به دوام الذكر واتصاله

TABRISI:7:205-206/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:205-206/r6.claim: Another explanation singles out these times because the heart is free from earning a livelihood and remembrance then takes firmer root.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r6.anchor: وقيل: إنما خص هذين الوقتين لأنهما حال فراغ القلب عن طلب المعاش فيكون الذكر فيهما ألصق بالقلب

TABRISI:7:205-206/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:205-206/r7.claim: The prohibition concerns neglecting the commanded supplication and remembrance.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r7.anchor: عما أمرتك به من الدعاء والذكر

TABRISI:7:205-206/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r8.speaker: ابن زيد ومجاهد وابن جريج
TABRISI:7:205-206/r8.claim: The verse may instead address those told to listen quietly to the Quran, who used to raise their voices with supplication when they heard mention of Paradise or Hell.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r8.anchor: وكانوا إذا سمعوا القرآن رفعوا أصواتهم بالدعاء عند ذكر الجنة أو النار عن ابن زيد ومجاهد وابن جريج

TABRISI:7:205-206/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r9.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:7:205-206/r9.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the verse shows that people who raise their voices in supplication are mistaken and contrary to the right course.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r9.anchor: قال الجبائي: وفي الآية دليل على أن الذين يرفعون أصواتهم عند الدعاء ويجهرون به مخطئن

ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r1.claim: الآصال means evenings; it is the plural of أصل, itself the plural of أصيل, hence a plural of a plural.
ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r1.anchor: الآصال جمع. أصل، والأصل جمع أصيل، فالآصال جمع الجمع. والآصال العشيات.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r2.claim: Remembering God inwardly means knowing what one is saying rather than speaking while heedless; “below audible speech” means hearing oneself without raising one's voice.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r2.anchor: ومعنى قوله تعالى (واذكر ربك في نفسك) أن تعلم ما تقول أي لا تذكر ربك وقلبك غافل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r3.claim: Taḍarruʿ is humility and abasement; khīfah here is likewise described as humble supplication and entreaty.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r3.anchor: وتضرعاً من التضرع والخيفة وهو بمعنى التذلل والتمسكن والمسكنة والتوسل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r4.claim: Khīfah may be a noun denoting a manner or an inward state, or a verbal noun; the source compares قتلة/قتلة, جرح/جرح, حمل/حمل, دهن/دهن, and وقود/وقود.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r4.anchor: الخيفة يجعلونها إما إسماً مثل الدُهن والجُرح وإما أن تكون الهيئة أي الشي الذي تجده في نفسك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says remembrance occurs only through tongue movement, taking “below loud speech” as secret, quiet verbal remembrance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والجمهور على أن الذكر لا يكون في النفس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān finds no proof for Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s claim; the verse distinguishes inward remembrance from remembrance by the tongue.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r2.anchor: ولا دلالة في ذلك لما زعم بل الظاهر المغايرة بين الحالتين وأنهما ذكران نفساني ولساني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says speaking below a loud voice deepens sincerity and lies closer to the nature of reflection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r3.anchor: ولذلك قال الزمخشري ومتكلما كلاما دون الجهر لأن الإخفاء أدخل في الإخلاص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r4.claim: One view restricts the two times to the periods when Muslims prayed twice daily, before the five prayers were prescribed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r4.anchor: فقيل: أراد خصوصية الوقتين لأنهم كانوا يصلون في وقتين قبل فرض الخمس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r5.claim: Qatāda identifies al-ghudū with the dawn prayer and al-āṣāl with the afternoon prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: الغدو صلاة الصبح والآصال: صلاة العصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r6.claim: Another view says dawn and evening are singled out because of their special merit.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r7.claim: The times may instead mean all times, with the two endpoints expressing the day and night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r7.anchor: وقيل: المعنى جميع الأوقات وعبر بالطرفين المشعرين بالليل والنهار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r8.claim: Some take al-ghudū as the plural of ghudwa, making it plural to match a generic noun in the contrast.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r8.anchor: والغدو، قيل: جمع غدوة فعلى هذا تظهر المقابلة لاسم جنس بجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r9.claim: If al-ghudū is the verbal noun of al-ghadāʾ, it means the times of early day, balancing one aggregate time span against another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r9.anchor: وإن كان مصدر الغداء فالمراد بأوقات الغدو حتى يقابل زمان مجموع بزمان مجموع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r10.speaker: أبو مجلز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r10.claim: Abū Mujliz reads wa-l-īṣāl as a verbal noun of āṣala, meaning entry into the late afternoon, parallel to other verbs for entering a time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز لا حق بن حميد السدوسي البصري والإيصال جعله مصدرا لقولهم آصلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r11.claim: The prohibition reinforces the command to remember: maintain remembrance and do not lapse into heedlessness even for an instant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r11.anchor: ولما أمره بالذكر أكد ذلك بالنهي عن أن يكون من الغافلين أي استلزم الذكر ولا تغفل طرفة عين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r12.claim: Although the Prophet cannot become heedless because of his protection from error, the prohibition is addressed to him with his community intended.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r12.anchor: ومعلوم أنه عليه السلام تستحيل عليه الغفلة لعصمته فهو نهي له صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد أمته

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r6.claim: Remembering God inwardly may mean adorning oneself with whatever divine qualities one can take on, or following the Prophet as the model in 33:21.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r6.anchor: بأن تتحلى بما يمكن التحلي به من صفات الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r7.claim: Humility and awe vary according to the spiritual station.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r8.claim: Remember inwardly without making the remembrance publicly audible.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r8.anchor: ودون الجهر ) أي دون أن يظهر ذلك منك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r9.claim: “Mornings” signify the appearance of the spirit’s light, while “evenings” signify the dominance of the soul’s qualities.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r10.claim: The command means never to be heedless of witnessing essential unity.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r10.anchor: ولا تكن ) في وقت من الأوقات

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r11.speaker: بعض الأكابر
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r11.claim: Some spiritual masters assign inward, humble remembrance to those who have arrived at witnessing; quiet remembrance to travelers toward it; and vigilance to lower-ranking novices.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r11.anchor: وقال بعض الأكابر : إن قوله سبحانه وتعالى : ( واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة ) إشارة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r12.claim: Fear signals awe of divine majesty; the cited poem says the speaker lowers his gaze from reverence, not fear, to protect beauty.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r12.anchor: أشتاقه فإذا بدا أطرقت من إجلاله لا خيفة بل هيبة وصيانة لجماله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r13.speaker: السهروردي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r13.claim: Al-Suhrawardī says the beginner’s or traveler’s method depends on the shaykh, a heart physician who may prescribe vocal remembrance to interrupt distracting thoughts.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r13.anchor: وفي عوارف المعارف للسهروردي قدس سره لا يزال العبد يردد هذه الكلمة على لسانه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r14.speaker: السهروردي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r14.claim: Al-Suhrawardī describes repeating the dhikr aloud with the heart accompanying it until it displaces inner speech; when the heart absorbs it, remembrance becomes witnessing, unveiling, and direct vision, the aim of retreat.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r14.anchor: حتى تصير متأصلة فيه مزيلة لحديث النفس وينوب معناها في القلب عنه فإذا استولت الكلمة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r16.speaker: السهروردي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r16.claim: Al-Suhrawardī compares the body to a city, its limbs to inhabitants, and the accomplished rememberer to a caller whose tongue awakens the heart and bodily parts until the heart’s light adorns the body with good works.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r16.anchor: ونقل عنه أيضا ما حاصله أن بنية العبد تحكي مدينة جامعة وأعضاؤه وجوارحه بمثابة سكان المدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p157/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p157/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p157/r10.claim: After al-Aʿrāf calls the Qurʾān guidance and mercy and commands listening and remembrance, al-Anfāl describes believers whose faith grows when its verses are recited and who trust God.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r4.claim: Other verses speak of inward secrets, remembering God inwardly, and what people say within themselves; in 3:167 that inward-speech reading is the most immediate sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r4.anchor: أي يقولون في أنفسهم كما هو الأسرع إنسياقا إلى الذهن والآيات في ذلك كثيرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas understands remembrance as recitation during prayer, quietly to oneself.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني بالذكر: القراءة في الصلاة، يريد يقرأ سرا في نفسه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r2.claim: The worshipper should implore God and fear Him in the quiet prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r2.anchor: {تضرعا وخيفة} خوفا، أي: تتضرع إلي وتخاف مني هذا في صلاة السر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r3.claim: In audible prayer, recitation should not be excessively loud; keep it low and calm but audible to those behind.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r3.anchor: وقوله: {ودون الجهر من القول} أراد في صلاة الجهر لا تجهر جهرا شديدا، بل في خفض وسكون، يسمع من خلفك،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r4.speaker: مجاهد وابن جريج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r4.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj say the command is to remember God inwardly through humble supplication without raising the voice or crying out.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد وابن جريج: أمر أن يذكروه في الصدور بالتضرع إليه في الدعاء والاستكانة دون رفع الصوت والصياح بالدعاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r5.claim: الغدو means early morning and الآصال evenings; أصيل, its singular, is the time between afternoon prayer and sunset.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321/r5.anchor: {بالغدو والآصال ولا تكن من الغافلين} أي: بالبكر والعشيات، واحد آصال: أصيل مثل يمين وأيمان، وهو ما بين العصر والمغرب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r1.claim: Remembrance privately covers recitation, supplication, and other forms; al-Shāfiʿī takes it as quiet recitation by a congregant after the imam finishes.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r1.anchor: عام في الأذكار من القراءة والدعاء وغيرهما

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r2.speaker: الشافعي
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r2.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī applies the command to a congregant reciting quietly after the imam finishes.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r2.anchor: كما هو مذهب الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r3.claim: The worshipper is humble and fearful, speaking above a whisper but below a raised voice, which supports humility and sincerity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r3.anchor: فوق السر ودون الجهر فإنه أدخل في الخشوع والإخلاص

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r4.claim: The phrase refers to morning and evening times.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r5.claim: A variant reads al-īṣāl, the verbal noun for entering late afternoon, matching the morning term.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r5.anchor: «والايصال» وهو مصدر آصل إذا دخل في الأصيل

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r6.claim: The warning is against being heedless of God’s remembrance.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r1.claim: Remember the Lord inwardly with understanding and practice; concealed remembrance better supports sincerity, reflection, and vigilant awareness of divine nearness.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r1.anchor: أي ذكرا يكون راسخا فيك مظروفا لك

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r2.claim: Remembrance should express humility without loud clamoring, like discreet speech to a ruler; a voice below public loudness better serves sincerity.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r3.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r3.claim: The Prophet told companions who had raised their voices excessively that they were not calling someone deaf or absent.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r3.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم للصحابة وقد جهروا بالدعاء فوق المقدار

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r4.claim: Verbal remembrance helps the heart remember; hearing oneself is enough to affect imagination and strengthen inward remembrance.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r4.anchor: فإن المقصود حصول الذكر اللساني ليعين الذكر القلبي

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r5.claim: As remembrance deepens, its lights reflect and increase, carrying the seeker from bodily darkness toward the light of the Lord of light and darkness.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r5.anchor: ولا تزال الأنوار تتزايد فينعكس تراجع بعضها إلى بعض حتى يزداد الترقي من ظلمات عالم الأجسام إلى أنوار مدبر النور والظلام

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r6.claim: Biqāʿī suggests الغدو is singular as a verbal noun of غدا; another view treats it as the plural of غدوة, including morning and forenoon.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r6.anchor: أي أوقات البكر , ولعله أفرده علىجعله مصدر غدا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r7.claim: A second grammatical account takes الغدو as plural of غدوة, so it can include the morning and forenoon.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r7.anchor: وقيل : الغدو وجمع غدوة , فيراد حينئذ مع الصبح الضحى

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r8.claim: Aṣīl names the end of each day because it joins the beginning of the following night and day.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r8.anchor: وآخر كل نهار متصل بأول ليلة اليوم الثاني فسمي آخر اليوم أصيلا لأنه يتصل بما هو أصل اليوم الثاني

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r9.claim: Although the command means constant remembrance, it names dawn and evening as parts representing the whole day and night: dawn recalls emergence from death, evening stillness and return to nonexistence.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r9.anchor: وخص هذين الوقتين وإن كان المراد الدوام بتسمية كل من اليوم والليل باسم جزئه , ليذكر بالغدو الانتشار من الموت

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r10.claim: The two named times do not restrict the command: remember God at every time and in every state.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r10.anchor: أي في غيرهما , بل كن ذاكره في كل وقت على كل حال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r2.claim: The address to the Prophet extends to the whole community and commands remembrance, glorification, praise, and sanctification of God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r2.anchor: مخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تعم جميع أمته وهو أمر من الله عز وجل بذكره وتسبيحه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r3.speaker: جمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r3.claim: The majority hold that remembrance “within oneself” still requires movement of the tongue, as indicated by “below the loudness of speech.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r3.anchor: والجمهور على أن الذكر لا يكون في النفس ولا يراعى إلا بحركة اللسان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r4.claim: The phrase describes the level of quiet, spoken remembrance rather than silent thought.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r6.claim: Khīfatan derives from khawfatan, with wāw changed to yāʾ because of the preceding kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r6.anchor: وخيفة أصلها خوفة بدلت الواو ياء لأجل الكسرة التي تقدمتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r7.claim: The phrase means to remember God continually, every day, and at the day’s two ends.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r7.anchor: وقوله بالغدو والآصال معناه دأبا وفي كل يوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r8.claim: One group says the verse describes Muslim prayer before the five daily prayers were made obligatory.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r8.anchor: وقالت فرقة هذه الآية كانت في صلاة المسلمين قبل فرض الصلوات الخمس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r9.claim: Qatāda identifies al-ghudu as the dawn prayer and al-āṣāl as the afternoon prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: «الغدو» صلاة الصبح والآصال صلاة العصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r10.claim: Al-āṣāl is a plural of aṣl, itself a plural of aṣīl, and may also be a direct plural of aṣīl or a plural of a plural, like īmān from yamīn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r10.anchor: والآصال جمع أصل والأصل جمع أصيل وهو العشي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r1.claim: The author reports Abū Majliz’s reading “والإيصال” as a verbal noun parallel to “الإصباح” and “الإمساء,” meaning entry into late afternoon.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r2.speaker: أبو وائل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits Abū Wāʾil asking his servant, “Have we entered evening yet?” as an example of the verb aṣala.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r2.anchor: وفي الطبري قال أبو وائل لغلامه هل آصلنا بعد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r3.claim: After warning against heedlessness, God gives the angels as an example of exertion to encourage earnest obedience.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r3.anchor: ولما قال الله عز وجل ولا تكن من الغافلين جعل بعد ذلك مثالا من اجتهاد الملائكة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r1.claim: The command to remember God at daybreak and evening parallels the command to glorify Him before sunrise and sunset.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r1.anchor: يأمر تعالى بذكره أول النهار وآخره، كما أمر بعبادته في هذين الوقتين في قوله: {وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل الغروب}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r2.claim: This Meccan verse preceded the institution of the five daily prayers on the Night Journey.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r2.anchor: وقد كان هذا قبل أن تفرض الصلوات الخمس ليلة الإسراء، وهذه الآية مكية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r3.claim: Al-ghudu means the beginning of the day; al-asal is the plural of asil, just as al-ayman is the plural of yamin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r3.anchor: بالغدو -وهو أوائل النهار: {والآصال} جمع أصيل، كما أن الأيمان جمع يمين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r4.claim: Remember God inwardly with fear and hope, and remember Him in speech without raising the voice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r4.anchor: أي: اذكر ربك في نفسك رهبة ورغبة، وبالقول لا جهرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r5.claim: When people asked whether to call upon a near Lord quietly or a distant Lord aloud, God revealed that He is near and answers supplication.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r5.anchor: فقالوا: أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه؟ فأنزل الله: {وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r6.claim: Abu Musa reports that during travel people raised their voices in supplication; the Prophet told them to be gentle, since they invoke One who hears and is near.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r6.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: رفع الناس أصواتهم بالدعاء في بعض الأسفار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r7.claim: The instruction may also echo 17:110: keep recitation moderate because polytheists insulted the Qur'an, its Sender, and its Messenger when they heard it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r7.anchor: وقد يكون المراد من هذه الآية كما في قوله تعالى: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r8.speaker: ابن جرير وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r8.claim: They construe the verse as telling a listener of Qur'an to remember in this manner while listening; Ibn Kathir rejects this as contrary to the command to listen attentively.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r8.anchor: وقد زعم ابن جرير وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم قبله: أن المراد بهذه الآية: أمر السامع للقرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir instead takes the verse to urge abundant remembrance by worshippers at daybreak and evening so they do not become heedless.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r9.anchor: بل المراد الحض على كثرة الذكر من العباد بالغدو والآصال، لئلا يكونوا من الغافلين

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r1.speaker: العامة
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r1.claim: The common reading khīfatan is a verbal noun from fear.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r1.anchor: قرأ العامة وخيفة: فعلة من الخوف،

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r2.claim: Some read khifyatan, on the pattern faʿla, from the verb meaning to conceal.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r2.anchor: وعن بعضهم (خفية) على وزن (فعلة) من الإخفاء.

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says āṣāl is a plural of aṣīl, itself pluralized first as aṣl: a plural of a plural.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r3.anchor: الآصال جمع، واحدها: أصيل، يجمع على أصل، ثم يجمع على آصال، فهو جمع الجمع، عن الزجاج.

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r4.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r4.claim: Another analysis takes āṣāl as a direct plural of aṣīl, like yamīn and aymān.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: الآصال جمع أصيل، ك يمين وأيمان.

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r5.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r5.claim: Āṣāl can mean the time between afternoon prayer and sunset; aṣīl has the diminutive aṣīlāl.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: الآصال: ما بين العصر والمغرب، والأصيل تصغيره أصيلال،

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r6.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r6.claim: The cited poetic line uses aṣīlāl in asking a dwelling for an answer, illustrating the time-word’s usage.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r6.anchor: قال الشاعر: وقفت فيها أصيلالا أسائلها ... عيت جوابا وما بالربع من أحد

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r7.claim: Aṣīl may derive from aṣl because it marks the point at which day ends and night begins, the origin of both.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو مأخوذ من الأصل الذي ينتهي إليه النهار وينشأ عنه الليل،

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r10.claim: Tadarruʿ means humility and weakness; the idiom ‘the fever humbled me’ illustrates the sense.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r10.anchor: والتضرع: التذلل والضعف، يقال: الحمى أضرعتني أي: ذللتني وضعفتني.

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r11.claim: After the preceding command to recite and listen to the Quran, these verses explain the manner of remembrance and supplication.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r11.anchor: لما تقدم الأمر بقراءة القرآن والاستماع، بين كيفية القراءة وكيفية الدعاء، فقال سبحانه: واذكر ربك

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r12.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r12.claim: Abu Muslim connects this to ‘My protector is God’ and takes it as a command to tell them to remember God.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r12.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: هذا يتصل بقوله: (إن وليي الله) أي: قل لهم هذا، وقل: اذكر الله،

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r13.claim: One view takes the command as addressed to the Prophet, while its intended scope is general.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r13.anchor: قيل: واذكر خطاب للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والمراد عام،

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r14.claim: Another view addresses every person and means to reflect on the signs and proofs in order to know God and His attributes.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r14.anchor: قيل: أراد واذكر أيها الإنسان ربك في نفسك قيل: تفكر في الآية وأدلتها لتحصل المعرفة به وبصفاته،

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r15.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r15.claim: Other explanations take remembrance as obedience, memory opposed to forgetfulness, spoken remembrance, or supplication; Abu Ali reports the supplication view.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r15.anchor: وقيل: اذكره بالطاعة، وقيل: هو الذكر الذي هو ضد النسيان، وقيل: أمرنا بالذكر الذي هو القول، وقيل: أراد به الدعاء، عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r16.speaker: ابن عباس والأصم
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r16.claim: Some take remembrance as prayer or Quran recitation in prayer; the author prefers this because the verse specifies remembrance short of aloud speech.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r16.anchor: وقيل: هو أمر بالصلاة، وقيل: بالقراءة في الصلاة، عن ابن عباس والأصم، وهو الأولى لقوله: ودون الجهر من القول،

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r17.claim: Remembering God inwardly is singled out because it is farther from ostentation.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r17.anchor: وإنما خص الذكر في النفس؛ لأنه أبعد من الرياء،

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r18.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r18.claim: Tadarruʿ is explained as humility and abasement; one reason for it is a shortcoming in fulfilling obligations.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r18.anchor: قيل: تخشعا وتذللا وهو لوجهين: أحدهما: يتضرع لتقصير وقع في واجباته.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r1.claim: Remembering God inwardly covers every kind of remembrance: Qurʾān recitation, supplication, glorification, tahlīl, and more.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r1.anchor: هو عام في الأذكار من قراءة القرآن والدعاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r2.claim: The two words mean that the worshipper is humble and fearful.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r3.claim: Speak below the level of public recitation; concealment deepens sincerity and better supports reflection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r3.anchor: ومتكلما كلاما دون الجهر ، لأن الإخفاء أدخل في الإخلاص

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r4.claim: The phrase may single out these two especially virtuous times or indicate continual remembrance; ghuduww means the morning hours.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r4.anchor: لفضل هذين الوقتين . أو أراد الدوام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r5.claim: A reading has والإيصال, from آصل ‘to enter the evening’; it parallels الغدو.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#3/r5.anchor: الإيصال ) ، من آصل إذا دخل في الأصيل
